items.title: Por que o Brasil ainda não sabe quantos entregadores se acidentam no trabalho?
items.summary: Principal obstáculo para medir o tamanho dos riscos é a falta de dados oficiais que permitam identificar se uma pessoa acidentada estava trabalhando no momento da ocorrência
items.body_text:
Por que o Brasil ainda não sabe quantos entregadores se acidentam no trabalho?
Após um acidente, o entregador Silvio Luiz Pinheiro pensou em desistir da profissão.
Quando entrou na central para devolver uma bicicleta alugada, ele ainda estava machucado. O ombro doía, o braço quase não acompanhava os movimentos.
Pouco antes, na Avenida Sumaré, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo, o freio dianteiro da bicicleta elétrica havia travado de repente. Ele precisou desviar de pedestres que estavam no meio da ciclovia. Com areia perto da pista, a bicicleta perdeu a estabilidade, e ele caiu.
"Para não machucar o rosto, eu coloquei o braço esquerdo na frente, um reflexo natural que a gente tem", conta.
Ele levou a bicicleta alugada até o balcão da central de locação, em Pinheiros, também na Zona Oeste da capital paulista, explicou que estava devolvendo o equipamento porque havia sofrido um acidente e esperou alguma reação.
Os funcionários fizeram os procedimentos necessários, confirmaram a devolução e encerraram o atendimento. A preocupação parecia ser apenas uma: registrar que a bicicleta havia voltado, diz ele.
Este foi o momento em que Silvio quase desistiu da profissão. "Foi uma coisa muito fria", lembra. "A preocupação deles é você devolver a bicicleta, pagar e não gerar muita preocupação para o aplicativo."
O resultado foi a clavícula e o cotovelo machucados, e uma recuperação mais lenta do que imaginava. "Eu achava que era uma lesão leve. Mas depois eu percebi que mexer com o ombro foi difícil até para voltar a fazer atividade física", diz. Hoje, ele avalia que está "99,9%" recuperado.
A experiência fez Silvio abandonar temporariamente as entregas e voltar a um emprego de carteira assinada em um restaurante. "Voltei para a CLT por causa do convênio, porque a plataforma não te dá essa segurança."
Hoje, ele voltou às entregas por aplicativo, atraído pelos benefícios de saúde do ciclismo. Pré-diabético, descobriu que passar o dia pedalando o ajudava a controlar o peso. E também lhe devolveu um prazer antigo, já que gosta da bicicleta muito antes de ela virar instrumento de trabalho.
Silvio gosta de trabalhar depois das 20h, quando os carros deixam de disputar cada centímetro de asfalto. Há menos motoristas, menos calor e, segundo ele, um risco menor de voltar para casa machucado.
Geralmente, sua jornada se estende até meia-noite. Em dias bons, continua pedalando até uma ou duas da manhã pelos bairros da República, da Santa Cecília e da Barra Funda.
O acidente mudou sua forma de enxergar o trabalho, mas não eliminou os riscos. Enquanto pedala, ele divide a atenção entre trânsito, pedestres e notificações do aplicativo, tentando equilibrar velocidade e segurança a cada cruzamento. Todos os dias, sai de casa com uma meta: faturar, idealmente, R$ 200. No mínimo, R$ 100.
"A gente anda com cuidado o tempo todo, mas é uma coisa que um dia pode acontecer. Desde que não seja fatal, pode acontecer com qualquer um."
Os acidentes que o Brasil não consegue contar
O trabalho por aplicativos segue em expansão no Brasil. Em 2024, eram 1,7 milhão de pessoas nessa modalidade, segundo o IBGE, o equivalente a 1,9% dos ocupados no setor privado. Em dois anos, houve um crescimento de 25,4%, com a entrada de mais 335 mil trabalhadores.
A maioria atua no transporte de passageiros: são 58,3% (964 mil). Já os entregadores representam 29,3% — ou seja, 485 mil pessoas. O grupo não é homogêneo: os trabalhadores que atuam em entregas se dividem principalmente pela idade e pelo veículo utilizado.
A renda média dos trabalhadores plataformizados, na época, era de R$ 2.996 com jornadas acima de 40 horas semanais. O rendimento médio da população brasileira atinge R$ 3.367 em 2025.
Medir o tamanho dos riscos que os entregadores enfrentam ainda é um desafio. O principal obstáculo é a falta de dados oficiais que permitam identificar se uma pessoa acidentada estava trabalhando no momento da ocorrência.

items.title: Como memórias da guerra e do passado nazista estão no centro de disputa eleitoral na Alemanha
items.summary: O partido de extrema-direita AfD acredita que o país deve adotar uma visão mais positiva de seu passado. Pela primeira vez, a legenda pode ganhar poder significativo na Alemanha no período pós-guerra.
items.body_text:
Como memórias da guerra e do passado nazista estão no centro de disputa eleitoral na Alemanha
  - Author, Jessica Parker
  - Role, Correspondente da BBC News em Berlim
  - Reporting from, Querfurt, Alemanha
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 7 min
Um partido que quer cortar o financiamento da arte "anti-alemã" e ensinar menos sobre Hitler às crianças, como parte de uma agenda "patriótica", poderá em breve chegar ao poder em um Estado da Alemanha.
Pesquisas de opinião apontam que o partido de extrema-direita Alternativa para a Alemanha (AfD) tem ampla vantagem nas intenções de voto no estado da Saxônia-Anhalt, antes das eleições estaduais de 6 de setembro.
Em seu manifesto, a legenda descreve a cultura da memória alemã — como são chamadas em português as políticas e práticas educacionais usadas para manter viva a lembrança dos crimes cometidos durante o nazismo no país —como um "complexo de culpa".
Trata-se de uma afirmação profundamente controversa em um país onde o enfrentamento dos crimes nazistas é visto há muito tempo como o alicerce moral da nação.
Num comício eleitoral na cidade de Querfurt, Gerd, de 70 anos, prendeu uma pequena bandeira alemã desfiada nas alças de sua scooter de mobilidade.
Não se pode "apagar" a história, diz o apoiador do AfD, mas "a Segunda Guerra Mundial não tem mais nada a ver conosco".
Gerd acredita que é importante olhar tanto para o futuro quanto para a história anterior à era nazista, quando as terras de língua alemã eram conhecidas como um lugar de "poetas e pensadores".
Caso chegue ao poder, a AfD quer mudar a forma como a história alemã é ensinada na Saxônia-Anhalt, um Estado localizado na região centro-leste do país.
O governo também se comprometeu a hastear a bandeira alemã todos os dias da semana nas escolas públicas e a preservar melhor os memoriais de guerra em homenagem aos soldados alemães.
Os demais partidos do Estado já afirmaram que não entrarão em coligação com a AfD, que é classificado como de extrema-direita em vários estados, incluindo a Saxônia-Anhalt, desde 2023.
A inteligência interna descobriu que a seção local do partido era antidemocrática e que seus objetivos eram permeados por uma "ideologia racista". A AfD geralmente rejeita essas classificações como difamações politizadas.
O objetivo do partido é conquistar votos suficientes para obter a maioria parlamentar na Saxônia-Anhalt: um feito notável na política alemã.
As pesquisas indicam que tal centário é possível.
Caso o partido consiga essa vitória, assumiria o controle de serviços como cultura, policiamento e educação.
A proposta é alterar o currículo de história escolar, dando mais ênfase ao século anterior em relação ao conflitos catastróficos da Primeira e da Segunda Guerra Mundial.
Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, idealizador do programa, afirmou que "é claro" que ainda haverá aulas sobre o Nacional-Socialismo, a ideologia política do partido comandado por Hitler, "mas em menor escala".
Em declarações a um programa da emissora pública ARD no ano passado, ele resumiu seu plano como "mais Bismarck, menos Hitler", referindo-se a Otto von Bismarck, o principal arquiteto da unificação alemã em 1871.
Figuras importantes da AfD já foram acusadas de tentar minimizar o capítulo mais sombrio da história alemã, em parte, segundo seus críticos, como forma de atrair seus apoiadores mais extremistas.
Em 2018, o ex-co-líder do partido, Alexander Gauland, comparou a era nazista a um "grão de cocô de passarinho", enquanto, um ano antes, Björn Höcke, que lidera o partido no Estado da Turíngia, descreveu o Memorial do Holocausto de Berlim como um "monumento da vergonha".
Na Saxônia-Anhalt, o homem que pode se tornar o primeiro governador estadual do AfD, Ulrich Siegmund, defendeu a agenda patriótica do partido, dizendo à BBC que era "a coisa mais normal do mundo" as pessoas se orgulharem de seu país.
"Queremos recuperar isso", disse ele. "Temos uma história diversa, que remonta a centenas de anos, e queremos ensinar essa história em sua totali

items.title: Por que as imagens das inundações no Nepal e no Tibete não são mostradas na China e se sabe pouco sobre as vítimas no país
items.summary: Algumas das imagens mais dramáticas das enchentes ocorridas na quarta-feira (26/8) são escondidas do público na China
items.body_text:
Por que as imagens das inundações no Nepal e no Tibete não são mostradas na China e se sabe pouco sobre as vítimas no país
  - Author, Laura Bicker
  - Role, Correspondente da BBC News na China
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 6 min
As imagens dramáticas eram praticamente impossíveis de ignorar.
Uma torrente de água invadia o porto de Gyirong, uma das principais passagens de fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, e arrastava tudo em seu caminho, enquanto centenas de pessoas fugiam para salvar a vida.
As cenas, capturadas por câmeras de segurança, se espalharam rapidamente pelas redes sociais e chegaram às telas de todo o mundo.
Exceto na China.
Até o momento, apenas uma única imagem estática foi transmitida pelo principal telejornal estatal do país.
Também tem sido difícil encontrar o vídeo na internet chinesa, que é fortemente censurada.
É igualmente difícil encontrar publicações que descrevam as inundações repentinas que deixaram centenas de mortos e desaparecidos na última quarta-feira (26/8).
Pequim lançou uma operação de resgate em larga escala que envolve centenas de socorristas. O trabalho está em andamento, e o presidente Xi Jinping presidiu uma reunião de emergência com autoridades para coordenar os esforços.
Mas, ao comparar o conteúdo disponível na internet do país com o que grande parte do mundo tem visto online nos últimos dias, o bloqueio da China torna-se mais visível do que nunca.
A região do Tibete, anexada por Pequim na década de 1950, resistiu por muito tempo ao domínio do Partido Comunista Chinês.
Ao longo dos anos, a China reprimiu protestos, por vezes de forma violenta, e foi acusada de graves violações dos direitos humanos na região de maioria budista.
O país classificou o líder espiritual exilado, Dalai Lama, como um separatista.
Essa história significa que o próprio nome Tibete atrai a censura da China. E a sensibilidade de Pequim fica especialmente evidente em momentos como este.
Os noticiários trazem atualizações diárias sobre os desaparecidos e os mortos, e Pequim também tem divulgado informações sobre as operações de resgate, bem como sobre os perigos representados por um lago de contenção que corre o risco de transbordar.
No sábado (29/8), novas imagens divulgadas pela mídia estatal chinesa mostram equipes de resgate andando por um terreno baldio cheio de lama e pedras, enquanto tentam identificar pessoas presas.
Mas há poucos detalhes além disso. Não existem relatos de sobreviventes no Tibete e quase nenhuma filmagem gerada por usuários mostra os momentos da enchente e as consequências que ela causou.
Ainda não tivemos notícias das famílias aflitas dos desaparecidos. Tentar contatar as pessoas no local é praticamente impossível, mesmo em tempos normais.
Como jornalista que cobriu a Coreia do Norte, muitas vezes foi mais fácil para mim contatar entrevistados em Pyongyang do que na capital tibetana, Lhasa.
Na noite de quinta-feira (27/8), enquanto as manchetes globais davam destaque à devastação em um vale do Himalaia, a emissora estatal chinesa abriu seu principal boletim de notícias com o lançamento do novo livro de Xi, uma seleção de suas "obras mais importantes e fundamentais".
Jornalistas estrangeiros não podem viajar para o Tibete sem autorização do governo.
Temos apenas algumas horas para obter o máximo de informações possível sobre histórias importantes como esta, antes que vídeos sejam apagados e vozes acabem silenciadas.
Dependemos da mídia estatal, que até agora tem se concentrado em esforços de resgate incrivelmente dramáticos.
Equipes de busca especializadas escalam montanhas e penhascos, ou atravessam rios caudalosos para tentar chegar às áreas mais afetadas. Ainda não sabemos o que aconteceu depois, nem quem eles conseguiram salvar.
Isso não significa que Pequim esteja indiferente. Pelo contrário, o governo parece muito preocupado com a situação.
O primeiro-ministro chinês, Li Qiang, foi rapidamente enviado à região, onde inspeciona a remoção de escombros — uma visita rara do segundo líd

items.title: Crise demográfica reduz força de trabalho e amplia desafios econômicos em Cuba
items.summary: Cuba registrou em 2025 quase o dobro de mortes em relação ao número de nascimentos, aprofundando a crise demográfica que afeta o país. A tendência deve agravar ainda mais a já fragilizada economia da ilha.
items.body_text:
Economia
Crise demográfica reduz força de trabalho e amplia desafios econômicos em Cuba
Cuba registrou em 2025 quase o dobro de mortes em relação ao número de nascimentos, aprofundando a crise demográfica que afeta o país. A tendência deve agravar ainda mais a já fragilizada economia da ilha.
Cuba encerrou 2025 com apenas 68.064 nascimentos e 136 mil mortes. Além disso, mais de 245 mil pessoas deixaram o país, números que aprofundam um processo de envelhecimento populacional de longa data e que afeta todas as províncias cubanas.
A aceleração do declínio demográfico decorre de múltiplos fatores, explica à RFI o demógrafo Juan Carlos Albizu, do Centro Cristão de Reflexão e Diálogo de Cuba.
“O que está acontecendo do ponto de vista demográfico é uma resposta adaptativa da população à situação do país, que vive um desastre humanitário. Há uma queda acelerada da fecundidade e um êxodo populacional em massa em resposta à incapacidade de garantir as próprias condições de vida”, analisa.
“As tendências de mortalidade já existem há muito tempo, uma vez que a expectativa de vida em Cuba vem caindo desde 2013”, afirma o demógrafo. No entanto, ele ressalta que o aumento da mortalidade e a redução da expectativa de vida se intensificaram nos últimos anos.
Para o economista e ex-professor da Universidade de Havana Omar Everleny, esse cenário pode estar relacionado à política dos Estados Unidos em relação a Cuba.
“Muitas pessoas que poderiam ser tratadas com medicamentos ou outros recursos atualmente não têm acesso a eles. E isso se deve, em grande medida, ao estrangulamento imposto pelo governo dos Estados Unidos, embora esse não seja o único fator.”
Consequências econômicas
As consequências da crise demográfica são graves para a economia da ilha. Segundo Albizu, 80% dos emigrantes tinham entre 15 e 59 anos, faixa etária considerada fundamental para a atividade econômica.
“Isso comprometerá a disponibilidade de mão de obra qualificada no médio prazo. Além disso, acelera o fechamento da janela de oportunidade demográfica, um ativo que a economia poderia ter aproveitado se as condições adequadas tivessem sido garantidas”, afirma.
O envelhecimento populacional e a emigração contribuíram para uma expressiva redução da população em idade ativa de Cuba. Nos últimos cinco anos, esse grupo encolheu em 1.259.894 pessoas, passando de 6.866.435 trabalhadores em 2021 para 5.606.541 em 2025.
Embora Albizu, que também é economista, afirme que o envelhecimento demográfico não seja, por si só, uma má notícia, ele destaca que se trata de um fenômeno irreversível. Em sua avaliação, a única política coerente seria impulsionar o desenvolvimento econômico por meio de investimentos significativos, capazes de assegurar um crescimento sustentado da produtividade do trabalho e atender às necessidades crescentes da população. Como exemplos, ele cita os países nórdicos, além dos modelos adotados pela China e pelo Vietnã.
“No entanto, muitos autores argumentam que essa oportunidade já foi perdida em Cuba, porque a alta cúpula dirigente se entrincheirou em um modelo socialista que não serviu para outro propósito além de se manter no poder, enquanto a população continua sofrendo todo tipo de privação. Assim, o atual modelo econômico cubano não apenas está falido, como também atua como um obstáculo ao próprio progresso”, enfatiza Albizu.
Caso esse cenário persista, o especialista conclui que a pobreza continuará avançando e a emigração em massa seguirá em curso, enquanto as taxas de fecundidade e a expectativa de vida continuarão em declínio.
Albizu alerta ainda que a redução da população cubana dos atuais 9,4 milhões para 6 milhões de habitantes, projeção das Nações Unidas para 2100, poderá ocorrer muito antes do previsto, possivelmente já em 2050.

items.title: ‘Bicho Pedra Gente’: Lucina se junta ao poeta arrudA em álbum sensível e intimista
items.summary: Dupla lança ‘Bicho Pedra Gente’ embalada pelo violão acolhedor da cantora e compositora
items.body_text:
Augusto Diniz | Música brasileira
Jornalista há 25 anos, Augusto Diniz foi produtor musical e escreve sobre música desde 2014.
Augusto Diniz | Música brasileira
‘Bicho Pedra Gente’: Lucina se junta ao poeta arrudA em álbum sensível e intimista
Dupla lança ‘Bicho Pedra Gente’ embalada pelo violão acolhedor da cantora e compositora
A cantora, compositora e violonista Lucina, que marcou a música brasileira ao formar dupla com Luhli (1945-2018), lançou um sensível e intimista álbum com o poeta arrudA. O trabalho intitulado Bicho Pedra Gente reúne 13 músicas de parceria bem-sucedida e precisa.
As composições são delicadas e foram construídas pelos dois, ao longo de cerca de 10 anos, e abordam sobre a vida cotidiana, do contato com a natureza e reflexões da existência. “A poesia de arrudA é extremamente sintética, mas cheia de significados”, diz Lucina.
Para o poeta, as músicas foram feitas com liberdade e linguagem própria, “livre de formatos estabelecidos”, como na canção Nossas Mãos Conversam. “Lucina representa a excelência na arte de valorizar a poesia nas canções”, diz. “Ela é para mim uma referência na música brasileira, tanto na trajetória com Luhli como na carreira solo. É uma mestra da composição”, complementa arrudA.
Todas as faixas foram gravadas tendo como base o violão tocado por Lucina e sua voz. “Funcionou incrivelmente, pois o ouvinte tem a sensação de que eu estou cantando e tocando na sala, completamente pertinho”, disse a CartaCapital.
Complementam a instrumentação das faixas os seguintes instrumentistas: Lui Coimbra (cello), Chris Oyens (guitarra, baixo e bateria), Bruno Aguilar (baixo), Walter Villaça (violão e guitarra), Adriano Souza (teclado e piano), Jorge Mathias (baixo fretless), Sandro Moreno (percussão eletrônica), Nando Duarte (violão), Joana Queiroz (clarone e clarinete), Ney Marquesk (guitarra) e Pedro Marcondes (baixo). A produção musical é de Patrícia Ferraz.
“Para cada canção temos um músico convidado. A faixa mais carregada tem eu e mais dois músicos tocando”, explica Lucina a composição sonora do disco. “Esses músicos são artistas que admiro e que têm uma carreira consagrada. Eles criaram suas sonoridades com toda liberdade, apenas com pontuações que eu fiz aqui e acolá”, diz.
Para a cantora, o álbum Bicho Pedra Grande é um trabalho de suma importância na sua carreira. “Ele apresenta meu ponto de vista musical na cena contemporânea de uma forma bastante íntima”, finaliza.
2026 já começou
Às vésperas das eleições de 2026, o País volta a encarar um ponto de inflexão: o futuro democrático está novamente em jogo.
A ameaça bolsonarista não foi derrotada, apenas recuou. No Congresso, forças conservadoras seguem ditando o ritmo. Lá fora, o avanço da extrema-direita e os conflitos em Gaza, no Irã e na Ucrânia agravam a instabilidade global.

items.title: Segurança vira aposta eleitoral no Nordeste, com candidatos divididos entre mais polícia, inteligência e prevenção
items.summary: Análise de CartaCapital dos programas de governo dos postulantes aos Executivos locais identificou diferentes estratégias para enfrentar o avanço das facções
items.body_text:
Política
Segurança vira aposta eleitoral no Nordeste, com candidatos divididos entre mais polícia, inteligência e prevenção
Análise de CartaCapital dos programas de governo dos postulantes aos Executivos locais identificou diferentes estratégias para enfrentar o avanço das facções
Quatro dos cinco estados com as maiores taxas de homicídios estimados do País estão no Nordeste, segundo o Atlas da Violência 2026, elaborado pelo Ipea em parceria com o Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Ceará, Bahia, Alagoas e Pernambuco estão entre os cinco primeiros do ranking. O Rio Grande do Norte também aparece entre os estados com maiores taxas de mortes violentas intencionais, segundo o Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública 2026.
É neste cenário de violência persistente e expansão do crime organizado que os candidatos aos governos desses estados apresentam suas propostas para a segurança pública nas eleições de outubro. Análise de CartaCapital dos programas de governo dos postulantes aos Executivos locais identificou diferentes estratégias para enfrentar o avanço das facções, com promessas de reforço policial, expansão da inteligência, uso de tecnologia, mudanças no sistema prisional e maior articulação entre forças de segurança.
As diferenças entre os planos ganham outra dimensão quando se considera a forma como o crime organizado passou a atuar na região. Nas últimas décadas, o Nordeste se tornou um corredor estratégico para grandes facções nacionais, que passaram a disputar territórios, rotas de tráfico e mercados ilícitos com grupos surgidos na própria região. O Primeiro Comando da Capital, de São Paulo, e o Comando Vermelho, do Rio de Janeiro, ampliaram sua presença.
No Ceará, por exemplo, PCC e CV estão entre as principais forças do crime organizado, ao lado de grupos locais como os Guardiões do Estado. Em Pernambuco, a atuação de grupos nacionais se mistura a organizações com origem em estados vizinhos.
No Rio Grande do Norte, o Sindicato do Crime mantém protagonismo local em meio à disputa com grupos de alcance nacional. Já Bahia tem um cenário ainda mais fragmentado, com ao menos sete grupos genuinamente baianos convivendo ao lado do PCC, que atua no estado desde 2018.
Alguns postulantes aos governos locais concentram suas propostas na ocupação dos territórios e no aumento do efetivo. Outros priorizam inteligência, tecnologia e integração de bancos de dados. Há ainda quem proponha atingir diretamente o dinheiro das facções, por meio de investigações sobre lavagem de dinheiro, patrimônio e empresas usadas para financiar as organizações.
Um governador pode contratar policiais, equipar delegacias, criar estruturas de inteligência, investir em tecnologia, organizar a Polícia Penal, construir presídios e estabelecer mecanismos de cooperação com outros estados e com a União. Não pode, sozinho, por exemplo, criar crimes, aumentar penas ou modificar regras nacionais de telecomunicações.
Para Bruno Langeani, consultor sênior do Instituto Sou da Paz, a campanha eleitoral ainda reproduz parte do repertório tradicional da segurança pública, especialmente entre candidaturas de direita. “Existe um repertório bastante repetido: aumento de penas, endurecimento penal e defesa de uma polícia mais violenta. Essas propostas encontram eco numa população amedrontada, enquanto políticas de segurança que efetivamente funcionam recebem muito menos visibilidade”, afirma.
Segundo o pesquisador, há espaço para uma discussão mais orientada por evidências. Pesquisas do instituto, diz Langeani, mostram que a população prefere policiais mais preparados a simplesmente mais policiais e valoriza investigação, julgamento e punição dos criminosos em vez de uma lógica baseada na letalidade policial.

items.title: 19 candidates to contest Sokoto gov seat in 2027
items.summary: 19 candidates are set to contest the Sokoto governorship election in 2027, including incumbent Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto. Learn more about the race. Read More: https://punchng.com/19-candidates-to-contest-sokoto-gov-seat-in-2027/
items.body_text:
No fewer than 19 candidates have been listed to contest the Sokoto State governorship election scheduled for 2027, according to the list displayed by the Independent National Electoral Commission at its state office on Saturday.
The list, sighted by our correspondent during a visit to the commission’s office, showed candidates from various political parties jostling for the state’s top political office.
Among the political parties listed are the Action Alliance, Social Democratic Party, Action Peoples Party, Action Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Movement, Zenith Labour Party, All Progressives Grand Alliance, Peoples Redemption Party, New Nigeria Peoples Party, National Rescue Movement, African Action Congress, Accord, Young Progressives Party, National Democratic Party, Labour Party, National Democratic Congress, Peoples Democratic Party, and the All Progressives Congress.
Those listed include Aliyu Shamsudeen Ahmad of the NDC, Abdullah Sokoto Abubakar of the PDP, Manir Muhammad Dan’Iya of the ADC and the incumbent governor, Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, of the APC.
The development has widened the field ahead of the election, with the various candidates expected to commence or intensify consultations, mobilisation and other political activities as the 2027 poll approaches.
However, the PDP’s entry into the race has been clouded by the party’s unresolved internal crisis, with Abdullah Sokoto Abubakar listed as the candidate produced by the faction associated with the Wike/Bature camp.
Reacting to the development, the Publicity Secretary of the other PDP faction, Hassan Sahabi Sanyinnawal, said the group was studying the situation and would announce its position after due consideration.
“We are studying the situation carefully and will make our position known to the public soon,” Sanyinnawal said.
He also appealed to PDP supporters to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the disagreement within the party.
“We urge all our supporters to remain calm and patient. There is no need for anybody to panic or take any action in haste,” he added.
The internal developments within the PDP are expected to remain a major issue in the political build-up to the 2027 election, particularly as the party seeks to consolidate its position ahead of the poll.
With 19 candidates listed, the Sokoto governorship race is expected to witness a competitive campaign, with the APC, PDP, ADC and other parties seeking to win the support of voters across the state.

items.title: I learnt my son’s kidney was removed via phone call — Victim’s mother
items.summary: A mother recounts learning via phone call that her 22-year-old son’s kidney was allegedly removed by an organ harvesting syndicate in Abuja. Police investi Read More: https://punchng.com/i-learnt-my-sons-kidney-was-removed-via-phone-call-victims-mother/
items.body_text:
The mother of 22-year-old Samuel Ezekiel, whose kidney was allegedly removed after he was deceived by his friend, Emmanuel Ode, has revealed that she only learnt about the incident after receiving a phone call from someone who heard that her son had undergone the procedure.
The woman said she had no knowledge that her son had been taken to a hospital in Abuja, where his kidney was allegedly removed on April 24, 2026.
Ezekiel had earlier told journalists that Ode deceived him into believing that they were going to the hospital for another purpose before he was eventually taken to Wellington Hospital, Life Camp, Abuja, where his kidney was allegedly harvested.
According to the victim, Ode assured him that removing his kidney would not affect his health or ability to live normally.
He also alleged that his identity was changed to “Hassan Abubakar” during the process and that an affidavit was prepared at the Federal High Court before he was taken to the hospital.
The police later alleged that Ode recruited Ezekiel for the procedure and that the victim’s kidney was harvested for $1,250, equivalent to about N1.7m.
The Nigeria Police Force subsequently paraded Ode, two doctors and another suspect over an alleged organ-harvesting and human-trafficking syndicate operating around Abuja and Nasarawa State.
The suspects paraded were Ode, 23; Dr Benjamin Oyime, a 48-year-old nephrologist and consultant to Wellington Hospital; Dr Daniel Otukpa, a 53-year-old nephrologist and Acting Director of Clinical Services at the hospital; and David Idoko, 25.
The police said the suspects were arrested by operatives of the Special Tactical Squad during a sting operation at Auta Balefi, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, on August 19.
The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said Ode allegedly confessed during interrogation to recruiting victims under false pretences.
The police further alleged that the syndicate targeted vulnerable and uneducated young people, exploiting their financial difficulties to obtain consent for illegal organ harvesting.
Investigators also alleged that official documents, including victims’ names, National Identification Numbers, birth certificates, age declarations, affidavits and consent letters, were forged to facilitate the procedures.
But while the investigation was unfolding, Ezekiel’s mother said she was completely unaware that her son had undergone the procedure.
She said she was at her shop when someone called her and informed her that her son’s kidney had been removed.
“I was in the shop one day, and someone called me to say they heard that my son’s kidney had been removed,” she said while speaking to journalists on Friday.
The mother said she immediately contacted another of her sons to find out what had happened, but he initially told her that he knew nothing about the matter.
She said she later learnt from her younger son that Ezekiel had been taken to a hospital by Ode, prompting her to report the matter to the police.
She said, “So, later, he told me that the junior one told him that Emmanuel took him to a hospital and then went and removed his kidney. So, that was how I went to the police station to report the matter.”
The woman said her son did not give her any money after the procedure.
Asked whether Ezekiel brought any money home, she replied, “No, no, no.”
Ezekiel had earlier told journalists that the payment he received was in US dollars and that he handed the money to Ode for safekeeping before entering the theatre.
He alleged that after the operation, Ode changed the money and used part of it to buy two phones, two power banks and two Wi-Fi devices.
Ezekiel said Ode gave him one of each item and kept the other for himself.
The victim also said he remained in the hospital for about a week after the operation before being discharged and taken by Ode to a hotel, where they stayed for two days.

items.title: VIDEO: I’ll attend your 70th birthday, Obasanjo jokes about missing Olota’s 80th celebration
items.summary: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo lightheartedly promised to attend Olota of Ota’s 70th birthday but joked about missing his 80th, drawing laughter from g Read More: https://punchng.com/video-ill-attend-your-70th-birthday-obasanjo-jokes-about-missing-olotas-80th-celebration/
items.body_text:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo added humour and warmth to the 60th birthday celebration of the Olota of Ota, Oba Professor Abdulkabir Obalanlege, offering prayers for the monarch while delivering a lighthearted remark about future milestones.
Speaking in Yoruba during the anniversary event, the 89-year-old elder statesman reflected on his early-morning call to the traditional ruler before making a humorous pledge regarding the monarch’s future milestone birthdays.
“Kabiyesi, I called you this morning and prayed for you,” Obasanjo said in Yoruba.
Obasanjo drew laughter from guests when calculating the timeline of the monarch’s future birthday celebrations.
Noting that he would be 99 at the king’s 70th and nearly 110 at his 80th, Obasanjo playfully asked to be excused from the latter milestone.
“I’m here celebrating your 60th birthday. I’ll join you for your 70th birthday in 10 years, but for your 80th birthday, which is 20 years from now, ẹ yonda mi (you’ll excuse me); you’ll celebrate that one the way it pleases you,” Obasanjo said.
The remarks drew laughter from dignitaries, traditional rulers, and guests gathered to honour Oba Obalanlege on his diamond jubilee.
PUNCH Online earlier reported that at the event, Fuji legend King Wasiu Ayinde, popularly called legend K1 De Ultimate, prostrated fully to Obasanjo as he came on stage, in a moment that captured traditional Yoruba respect and cultural display.

items.body_text:
Rescuers in Nepal and China were battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing entire villages.
The latest figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 633 bodies recovered — and reports of some dead possibly swept downstream as far away as India.
Rescue worker Kawan Koirala, from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they were struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud.
“People want their want their family’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them… you can see the mud,” he told AFP, exhausted after an 18 hour shift.
“It is very traumatic for me too. It is my first time seeing these types of things. Everywhere is mud. We faced floods in Nepal before, but not like this.”
The US Geological Survey said the disaster on Wednesday on the Tibet-Nepal border was caused by a glacial collapse that created a torrent of debris downstream.
Those that made it out say they have lost everything and now face an agonising wait to discover the fate of missing loved ones, and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away. There is nothing left,” survivor Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP.
“There is nothing left.”
At Bidur’s army base, a key rescue hub in the same district, relatives crowded around lists of rescued people pasted on a wall.
Samjhana Thing said she had been waiting three days for news of her missing brother.
“We don’t know anything. Hopefully he is in a safe place,” she said.
“I have come here looking for my son,” said Kalka Sharda, scanning the list in desperation.
“He was a labourer at the hydropower plant, but I can’t find his name, and the authorities are not saying anything.”
In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority listed 933 hydropower workers among the missing, along with 517 foreigners, including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
Risk of lake burst near disaster site wanes
The threat of a lake formed after the glacier collapse has eased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday, as it appears to have shrunk.
Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake, which straddles the border between China’s Tibet region and Nepal at the confluence of two rivers, has been slowly flowing out and gradually reducing the reservoir, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the Water Resources Ministry.
By Saturday afternoon, parts of the lake bed had become visible, CCTV reported.
The ministry said satellite imagery of the lake on the Purepu Tsangpo river showed it covered 99,000 square metres early on Saturday, roughly the size of 14 soccer pitches, having shrunk by 21,000 square metres since Thursday.
‘Enormous’ trauma
The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous”, and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.
Emergency teams worked flat out to find survivors as widespread devastation left communities short of food and water.
Fears of further flooding have compounded the search for the missing.
The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes, and one of these formations has become a risk of further floods.
While the exact cause of the collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of such disasters.
In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing had paused its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding.
On the Nepali side, soldiers were trying desperately to drill through to 100 people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Saturday.
The prime minister’s office said teams had begun “clearing mud and debris” to open the entrance, while a specialised Indian tunnel rescue unit had arrived to help.

items.body_text:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Four cops were injured on Saturday when terrorists attacked a police party in the Hathala area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan district, police said.
In a statement, the district police spokesperson said that the police party, led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Kefayat, was on its way when terrorists fired at them near Pota and Al-Amin Farm House.
“Police retaliated, leading to an exchange of fire between the two sides,” the spokesperson said. During the exchange of fire, the police vehicle overturned, injuring several personnel, he added.
DPO Ziauddin Ahmed told Dawn that four policemen were injured in the incident, with one of them sustaining a bullet wound.
“The condition of all the injured is out of danger,” he said.
A heavy contingent from Ijaz Shaheed Police Lines reached the area following the attack, while officials cordoned off the area and launched a search operation.
Earlier this month, at least 14 people, lost their lives and 18 others were injured when a suicide bomber blew himself up near the Kabal Police Station in Swat.
According to the Annual Security Report 2025 from the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), KP recorded a significant surge in violence last year as “fatalities rose from 1,620 in 2024 to 2,331 in 2025”.
This marked an “absolute increase of 711 deaths, accounting for over 82 per cent of the net national rise and marking almost a 44pc year-on-year surge in violence in the province”.

items.body_text:
KARACHI: The South deputy inspector general (DIG) on Saturday said an investigation had been ordered after a video emerged of police’s alleged involvement in a recent scuffle between two apartment residents in Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 6.
In the CCTV footage, a woman can be seen rushing down a flight of stairs with a dumbbell in her hand and charging at another woman before using it to hit her.
The video also showed two individuals in what appeared to be police uniforms restraining the woman being assaulted, and a man who came up the stairs shortly after and began arguing with the woman with the dumbbell.
At one point, the man and woman being assaulted manage to go inside what appeared to be their home, following which the woman with a dumbbell and another man begin banging on their door and yelling obscenities.
At the end, a man in a shalwar kameez can be seen using a weapon, provided by one of the people in uniform, to smash the CCTV camera.
After CCTV footage surfaced online of the incident, South DIG Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that he had directed the investigation officer to conduct a probe on merit and in an impartial manner. He said that both sides had levelled accusations against each other.
Meanwhile, a first information report (FIR) of the incident, a copy of which is available with Dawn, was registered at Darakhshan police station at 1:40am on Aug 21 on the complaint of a woman. The FIR offered a different version of events.
It invoked sections 354 (assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), 506 (criminal intimidation), 337A(i) (punishment of shajjah), 382 (theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint to commit theft) and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code.
In the complaint, the woman described herself as a resident of the fourth floor of an apartment building, adding that a man, his sister and their mother — who resided on the third floor — came to their door and started kicking it.
The complainant alleged that the three family members hurled verbal abuses over a parking issue, and upon opening the door, began beating and threatening her.
Subsequently, local police arrived on the spot and took the brother and sister into custody on the complainant’s statement, while their mother fled, the FIR said.
In the FIR, the woman also claimed that the other side “snatched” her gold earring and two rings.
However, DIG Raza said that Section 382 pertaining to the alleged theft of gold ornaments had been removed from the FIR as the incident appeared to be a case of assault.

Published August 29, 2026
The Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy was sidelined for Friday’s preseason game at the Denver Broncos due to an ankle injury.
McCarthy’s injury forced coach Kevin O’Connell to sideline him earlier than expected from the Ravens game.
The Vikings quarterback McCarthy suffered an injury scare last weekend during a game against the Baltimore Ravens.
Vikings’ coach had earlier expressed hope earlier in the week that McCarthy could start against the Broncos for extra reps before the regular season gets underway.
“We hoped to get him turned over,” commented coach Kevin O’Connell after the Vikings’ 34-6 defeat to the Broncos.
“The goal was to have him start the game tonight and try to get him a half if we could…we just couldn’t get him there,” O’Connell added.
When coach O’Connell was asked where McCarthy ranked on the Vikings’ depth chart after the preseason ended, O’Connell said, "We're going to work through that as a staff and see where he’s at from a health standpoint first and foremost. We don’t have any long-term concerns.
“Still consider him day to day, and we’ll see what that looks like.”
Vikings starter Kyler Murray was already set to sit out, along with most of Minnesota’s key starters.
That left Carson Wentz and second-year quarterback Max Brosmer as the available roster options in Denver.

items.title: Remand of suspects in Hina Javed murder case extended
items.summary: Representational image of a gavel placed on a wooden table in a court. — Reuters/FilePolice present Asghar, Zeeshan before court.Rawalpindi court adjourns hearing till Sep 2.Police seek seven-day extension in suspects’ remand.A district and sessions court in Rawalpindi...
items.body_text:
Published August 29, 2026
- Police present Asghar, Zeeshan before court.
- Rawalpindi court adjourns hearing till Sep 2.
- Police seek seven-day extension in suspects’ remand.
A district and sessions court in Rawalpindi on Saturday extended the physical remand of two suspects, Faisal Asghar, husband of slain Hina Javed, and domestic worker Zeeshan, by another four days for further investigation into her murder.
Hina, a digital media executive, was found dead at her home in Rawalpindi’s Lalkurti area, with her body tied to a shower in the bathroom on August 20.
At the outset of today’s hearing, police presented the suspects before the court after the expiry of their three-day physical remand.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Rehman Shaukat Bhatti appeared before the court on behalf of the police and sought a seven-day physical remand of the suspects, saying they needed to recover documents related to Asghar’s divorce from his first wife and his marriage to the slain woman.
After hearing the arguments, the court granted the police a three-day physical remand of the suspects and ordered them to produce them before the court on September 2.
During the previous hearing on August 26, Advocate Shah Khawar, counsel for the deceased’s family, had told the media that police investigation was proceeding in the right direction.
“The police have collected evidence and conducted forensic examinations. In my view, the investigation is moving in the right direction,” he had said.
The development comes two days after the domestic worker confessed to strangling and torturing Hina Javed.
The arrested worker had told investigators he had been called during a marital dispute between Hina and her husband Faisal, according to sources.
He had said Hina tried to flee during the altercation, upon which Faisal and he grabbed her. When she resisted, he pressed her throat, he had confessed. Zeeshan also admitted to frequently stealing from the household.
According to police sources, Hina's father-in-law had called police saying thieves had broken into the house. When police arrived, they found Hina's body tied to a shower in the bathroom.
The post-mortem report of Hina has revealed injuries to several parts of the victim's body.
According to the report, Hina's neck bone was fractured, while injury marks were also found on her ribs and hip bone.

A family living in Defence Phase 6, Karachi, has been forced to leave its apartment and move elsewhere after an alleged assault involving an influential woman and police personnel.
The incident took place on 21 August. According to reports, Maryam Ali Raza allegedly assaulted a brother and sister with a dumbbell in the presence of police officers.
She later filed a first information report (FIR) against Ahsan, Noor-ul-Ain and their mother at Darakshan police station.

ARY News has reported that Maryam Ali Raza is a relative of Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Fida Hussain Janwari.
Following the incident, the affected family reportedly left the apartment because of concerns for their safety.
Residents of the area have alleged that the woman, identified as Maryam, also runs the building’s union and prevents other residents from using the lift.
Ali Ahsan, who lived in the apartment with his mother and sister, had also submitted an application to Darakshan police station concerning the building’s management.
In the complaint, he said the family had been living in the building since November 2021.
Ahsan said they had been unable to hire a separate security guard and had therefore installed a security camera. He alleged that Maryam had also threatened to cut off their electricity supply.
He said the family had approached the police over the dispute and requested protection.

items.title: Deep Earth surface mapped by scientists using new AI technology
items.summary: Deep Earth surface mapped by scientists using new AI technology
items.body_text:
Deep Earth surface mapped by scientists using new AI technology
- By Kumail Shah -
- Aug 29, 2026
Far below the Earth’s surface, where the solid mantle touches the molten outer core, scientists have found almost 175,000 seismic signals that had never been recorded before. This is over ten times as much as earlier studies found.
Researchers at the Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, created a new deep learning tool to spot PKP precursors—faint seismic waves that appear just before stronger ones as they bounce off irregularities near the core-mantle boundary.
The team, whose findings will appear in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth in 2026, trained their algorithm using over 2 million seismic waveforms from around 5,000 earthquakes recorded between 1990 and 2024.
By repeatedly correcting its mistakes, they enabled the system to analyze data on a scale that would be impossible for humans to process by hand.
Previous maps of the deepest part of the mantle showed these anomalies scattered at random. With the much larger dataset, scientists now see that most of these once-isolated patches are actually linked together, forming broad bands along the core-mantle boundary.
These bands might include fragments of oceanic crust and sediment that have sunk deep into the Earth over millions of years. Some could be associated with extended low shear-velocity zones, often called ‘blobs,’ or with debris from the ancient collision that led to the formation of the Moon.
Under the immense pressure at these depths, this material can melt or transform into minerals that differ markedly from the surrounding rock.
The researchers have found six regions that have not been studied extensively before, such as high-latitude Eurasia, Central Asia, and the South Atlantic. They see these as top priorities for future research using different seismic wave methods.
The study flags six previously under-sampled regions, including zones beneath high-latitude Eurasia, Central Asia, and the South Atlantic, as priorities for future research using several types of seismic waves.

items.title: Sindh govt, KWSC ordered to pay Rs15m over girl’s death in open manhole
items.summary: Sindh govt, KWSC ordered to pay Rs15m over girl’s death in open manhole
items.body_text:
Sindh govt, KWSC ordered to pay Rs15m over girl’s death in open manhole
- By Farooq Sami -
- Aug 29, 2026
KARACHI: A local court in Karachi on Saturday ordered the Sindh government and the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) to pay Rs15 million in compensation to the legal heirs of an eight-year-old girl who died after falling into an uncovered manhole, holding the authorities responsible for negligence.
The order was issued by Senior Civil Judge (West) Salman Amjad Siddiqui after hearing a compensation suit filed by the girl’s parents through their counsel, Advocate Farrukh Usman, under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855.
The parents had sought compensation from the Sindh government and KWSC, alleging that their daughter’s death was caused by the defendants’ negligence and failure to ensure public safety.
According to Advocate Farrukh Usman, the incident occurred in 2021 at Sher Muhammad Village near Mauripur Road.
He said the girl, identified as Habiba, had gone outside to play. Her body was found two days later in a nearby sewer, where the manhole cover was missing.
The parents had initially sought Rs25 million in damages and made the Sindh government and KWSC parties to the case.
After hearing the arguments and examining the evidence, the court held the concerned authorities liable for the incident and ordered them to pay Rs15 million in compensation to the deceased girl’s legal heirs.
Similar Compensation Order Issued in May
In a similar case, a local court in Karachi’s West district on May 20, 2026, ordered the Town Municipal Corporation (TMC) Orangi Town to pay Rs15 million in compensation to the legal heirs of a man who died after falling into an uncovered nullah during heavy rainfall.
Court orders TMC Orangi to pay Rs15m over man death in nullah
The court held TMC Orangi Town responsible for the fatal incident while clearing the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) of liability.
According to the petition, the deceased, identified as Arif, was returning home during heavy rainfall on July 26, 2020, when he fell into an uncovered nullah due to poor maintenance and inadequate safety measures.
He sustained serious injuries and died at the scene.

items.title: Punjab introduces new facility to track driving license delivery
items.summary: Citizens will be able to track their driving license cards online and check their current locations. The post Punjab introduces new facility to track driving license delivery appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
Punjab introduces new facility to track driving license delivery
				
				
					
Citizens will be able to track their driving license cards online and check their current locations.
				
		
				 
				
					
Punjab authorities have decided to integrate the Pakistan Post delivery system with the Traffic Police’s Driving License Information Management System, or DLIMS, to address delays in the delivery of driving license cards.
Under the proposed system, citizens will be able to track their driving license cards online and check their current locations.
Currently, DLIMS only shows whether a license card is being processed or printed. Once the two systems are connected, applicants will also be able to see when the card is handed over by the traffic police to Pakistan Post, its delivery status and its current location.
Officials said the traffic police also face difficulties tracking license delivery information under the existing system.
The Punjab Information Technology Board, or PITB, has been contacted to help integrate the two systems.
Authorities expect the new system to improve monitoring and transparency and help ensure that driving license cards are delivered to citizens within the prescribed time.

items.title: China’s top memory chipmaker sues Pentagon over military ties listing
items.summary: CXMT said it had spent more than a year providing information to U.S. officials in an effort to challenge the designation. The post China’s top memory chipmaker sues Pentagon over military ties listing appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
China’s top memory chipmaker sues Pentagon over military ties listing
				
				
					
CXMT said it had spent more than a year providing information to U.S. officials in an effort to challenge the designation.
				
		
				 
				
					
CHINA: ChangXin Memory Technologies, China’s leading memory chipmaker, sued the U.S. Department of Defense over its inclusion on a Pentagon list of Chinese companies, as Washington says it support Beijing’s military.
CXMT which makes dynamic random-access memory chips said in its lawsuit that it has no connection to China’s military and produces its chips for civilian and commercial customers.
The Pentagon declined to comment on the ongoing lawsuit. “As a matter of policy, the department does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation.”
The U.S. government first designated CXMT as a Chinese military company in January 2025 under the Biden administration. The Trump administration kept the company on the list in a June 2026 update.
CXMT said it had spent more than a year providing information to U.S. officials in an effort to challenge the designation and secure its removal from the list.
According to the lawsuit, the Defense Department published a notice in February saying CXMT would be removed from the list. The notice was withdrawn later that same day, the company said.
“None of these determinations is supported by the factual record, by applicable law, or by reasoned decision-making,” the company said in its complaint.
The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. CXMT is China’s largest maker of DRAM chips, which are widely used in smartphones, personal computers, servers, artificial intelligence systems and other electronic devices.
CXMT’s case follows a similar lawsuit filed by Chinese technology giant Alibaba in June. Alibaba challenged its inclusion on another Pentagon list that identifies Chinese companies.

items.title: DHA apartment fight raises questions over police role
items.summary: CCTV footage appears to show an attack and a man damaging a security camera during the Aug. 21 confrontation. The post DHA apartment fight raises questions over police role appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
KARACHI: A dispute at a DHA apartment has turned into a police controversy after CCTV footage appeared to show a woman attacking two neighbors with a dumbbell and a plainclothes man damaging a security camera, prompting authorities to launch an inquiry into the incident and the subsequent theft case against the victims.
The Aug. 21 confrontation took place at an apartment on Khayaban-e-Bukhari in Phase VI, where the female resident and her brother were allegedly assaulted before being arrested and booked at Darakshan police station, raising questions over whether police influence was used in the case.
The CCTV footage shows the woman repeatedly striking the female resident with a dumbbell during the confrontation. A man in plain clothes is also seen damaging a CCTV camera at the apartment.
Police sources and area residents identified the woman as Maryam Ali Raza and alleged that she is a relative of SSP Korangi Fida Hussain Janwari.
Residents claimed she had previously used her alleged police connections in disputes involving security guards and other residents. The allegations are part of the ongoing inquiry and have not been independently established.
Following the confrontation, the two siblings were arrested and a theft case was registered against them at Darakshan police station. The case later came under scrutiny after investigators reviewed the CCTV footage.
Police said the footage examined so far does not support the initial allegations of snatching or theft. The sections relating to snatching and theft have since been removed from the case, while officials said the challan would not be submitted until the inquiry is completed.
Police launch investigation
Deputy Inspector General South Asad Raza formed an investigation team headed by the SSP Investigation South to determine what happened and whether any police officials acted improperly.
Investigators will record statements from people visible in the CCTV footage and police personnel who were present at the apartment. They are also examining the available recordings and other evidence to establish the sequence of events.
Raza said the inquiry would be conducted strictly on merit and would examine all aspects of the incident, including the circumstances surrounding the registration of the case against Maryam Ali Raza.
Police officials said action would be taken against any officer or individual found responsible for bias, misconduct or irregularities in the case.
Plainclothes officer raises questions
The role of the man seen damaging the CCTV camera has also become a key part of the investigation. Police officials said he is allegedly a Korangi police officer and that the footage appears to show him using a service weapon to damage the camera.
His reported presence has raised questions because the apartment falls within the jurisdiction of Darakshan police station, not Korangi police.
Investigators are expected to question the officer and other police personnel seen in the footage to determine why they were at the apartment and whether they had any involvement in the confrontation or the subsequent case against the siblings.
Police said all available CCTV recordings, witness statements and other evidence will be reviewed before the inquiry reaches a final conclusion.

items.body_text:
Toxic Sulfur odor blankets Baghdad again: Warnings of health crisis
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A pungent, sulfur-like odor returned to envelope several residential districts across Baghdad overnight between Friday and Saturday, August 29, 2026, marking the latest wave of recurrent toxic air pollution that has triggered widespread public health concerns and resident complaints.
The recurrence comes less than three weeks after an intense sulfur plume blanketed southern and central Baghdad for 48 hours, prompting fresh warnings from the Green Iraq Observatory regarding untreated industrial emissions, unregulated open burning, and poor environmental oversight
According environmental evaluations by the Green Iraq Observatory, the recurrent pollution wave stems from a combination of industrial practices and meteorological dynamics:
- High-Sulfur Heavy Fuel Combustion: Heavy reliance on high-sulfur heavy fuel oil (HFO) and untreated crude derivatives across thermal power generation stations, brick kilns, and asphalt plants on the capital’s periphery.
- Al-Daura Refinery Smoke Plumes: Previous documentation captured heavy smoke discharges emanating from the Al-Daura refinery complex south of Baghdad, drifting over nearby urban neighborhoods.
- Informal Waste Incineration: Continuous unregulated burning of municipal plastic waste and uncontrolled open landfill fires surrounding the municipal perimeter.
- Thermal Inversion Trapping: Nocturnal and early-morning thermal temperature inversions create a dense atmospheric lid, preventing vertical dispersion and trapping toxic sulfur dioxide (SO2) and particulate matter near ground level.
The Green Iraq Observatory warned that the return of sulfur emissions within less than two weeks disproves official claims of containment, highlighting severe health ramifications:
- Surge in Respiratory Illness: Noticeable increases in bronchitis flare-ups, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and severe asthma attacks.
- High-Risk Demographics: Children, elderly residents, and individuals with pre-existing cardiopulmonary conditions face heightened vulnerabilities from prolonged particulate exposure.

items.summary: Iran said that 40 percent of the damaged capacity of the South Pars gas field has been restored, according to the semi-official news agency Fars – adding, however, that it will take at least two years to rebuild the facility attacked by Israel this year. “With the tools we have, we managed to restore about … The post Iran says 40% of capacity at its giant gas field has been restored appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Iran said that 40 percent of the damaged capacity of the South Pars gas field has been restored, according to the semi-official news agency Fars – adding, however, that it will take at least two years to rebuild the facility attacked by Israel this year.
“With the tools we have, we managed to restore about 40 percent of the damaged capacity. However, the damage that has been inflicted is very severe. It will definitely take at least two years of work just for those sites to be rebuilt,” Iran’s deputy oil minister, Ahmad Zeraatkar, told Fars on Thursday.
Iranian officials have acknowledged the desruptions to energy exports that are vital for government finances, but have sought to play them down.
Zeraatkar said that by targeting energy, the US and Israel seek to curtail the government’s ability to provide for the public.
Earlier this week, Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad acknowledged that oil sales have “decreased to some extent” during the US blockade, but said they have “continued” nonetheless.
South Pars is part of the world’s largest natural gas reserves, located offshore in the Persian Gulf. It is shared between Iran and Qatar, which calls its part of it the North Field.
In March, an Israeli strike on Iranian facilities in the South Pars gas field marked a significant escalation in the war, prompting a furious Iran to attack major energy facilities of its Gulf neighbors, sending oil prices surging, and leading US President Donald Trump to threaten to “blow up” South Pars if Iran didn’t stop.

items.title: She fled Iran. America sent her to Africa
items.summary: Bangui, Central African Republic — “It’s okay now, I’m safe,” she remembered thinking. “I can make one new life here.” She described her joy at reaching “one of the best countries in the world,” but her happiness would prove fleeting. Nika is among a growing number of migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries they’ve … The post She fled Iran. America sent her to Africa appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
“It’s okay now, I’m safe,” she remembered thinking. “I can make one new life here.”
She described her joy at reaching “one of the best countries in the world,” but her happiness would prove fleeting.
Nika is among a growing number of migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries they’ve never been to – countries that can hardly be considered safe havens. It’s a loophole. Judges have stopped the US government from sending some migrants back to their home countries. So it has inked dozens of arrangements with third countries, where people like Nika are increasingly festering. Because she fears for both her and her family’s safety, Nika is a pseudonym.
‘If I was in Iran, they’re going to kill me’
Telling her story for the first time, Nika says she spent much of her youth protesting against the Iranian regime.
“I lost too much of my friends. They [the Islamic Republic] killed them. And some of them are still in prison,” she said tearfully. “I know if I was in Iran, they’re going to kill me.”
Her story unfolds at a remarkable time in US-Iran relations. Earlier this year, Iran was rocked by widespread anti-government protests. The regime launched an unprecedented crackdown, killing thousands. President Donald Trump encouraged protesters to “take over your institutions” and said, “help is on its way.”
On the last day of February, the US and Israel launched a war on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and attacking targets across the country.
Nika followed the events closely from the United States. She allowed herself to hope it might mean the end of the Iranian regime, and a return home. In reality her fate had already been decided.
One of the hardest days
After being detained at the border and months in ICE detention, Nika had briefly been allowed to live freely in California. She received a Department of Homeland Security notice asking her to attend what she understood to be a routine meeting in June. But according to documents reviewed by CNN, US authorities had decided weeks earlier to deport her. When she attended the meeting, she was arrested.
Three days later, on the evening of June 11, she says she was handcuffed, shackled and placed on a deportation flight along with 17 other migrants, including those from Afghanistan, Iraq and Georgia.
“This is one of the very hard days in my life,” said Nika, describing how her whole body shook with fear. She said it was only on boarding the flight that she learned where she was going. The destination was shown on the small screen attached to the seat in front of her.
Sahar Jalili Pawelski, Nika’s current immigration lawyer, said she tried desperately to get her off the flight.
“I remember when the flight took off, I just sat on the floor, called my mom and cried. I live those moments. You know what that person must’ve been feeling. The loneliness she must have felt,” said Pawelski.
Legal protection
Like many of the other migrants she was deported with, Nika had won a protection order from an American judge. Such orders are intended to prevent migrants from being returned to places where they could face persecution, torture or death.
Until recently, it was extremely rare for people with these types of protection orders to be deported.
But since Trump returned to power last year, promising mass deportations, that’s all changed. Trump’s top anti-immigration advocate, deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, has stated “America’s doors are closed, fully, to asylum seekers.”
The Department of Homeland Security has defended its actions, telling CNN in a statement that those deported received due process and had final orders of removal.
“These third country agreements, which ensure due process under the U.S. Constitution, are essential to the safety of our homeland and the American people. We are applying the law as written. If a judge finds an illegal alien has no right to be in this country, we are going to remove them. Period.”

items.title: Trump is staking out extreme positions on White House secrecy, legal experts say
items.summary: At this point more than two months before the midterm elections, Democrats retaking control of Congress and its subpoena power is far from certain. But President Donald Trump is already laying down legal markers for how he’ll fight any attempt by lawmakers to investigate him. In a Justice Department memo and legal filings, the Trump … The post Trump is staking out extreme positions on White House secrecy, legal experts say appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
At this point more than two months before the midterm elections, Democrats retaking control of Congress and its subpoena power is far from certain. But President Donald Trump is already laying down legal markers for how he’ll fight any attempt by lawmakers to investigate him.
In a Justice Department memo and legal filings, the Trump administration is arguing that the president can keep secret not just the conversations he has with his advisers within the White House, but that his dealings with individuals outside the government can be shielded as well. The White House is also saying in court that even disclosing the identities of the people who worked on significant policy efforts would infringe upon the presidential confidentiality to which Trump is entitled. And the administration has taken the stance that it can ignore a Watergate-era law prohibiting the destruction of White House documents.
The posturing comes as Trump, in his second term, has been notably reliant on a constellation of business moguls, non-government attorneys and old friends to help shape his agenda.
“There has been an unprecedented amount of interaction between the Executive Branch — particularly the White House — and the private sector that Congress has made clear is going to be the subject of oversight,” said Jamie Bair, a partner and head of congressional investigations at the law firm Crowell & Moring.
Congressional Democrats are already probing the administration’s interactions with FIFA, how Trump’s ties to the crypto-industry are affecting federal policy, and other examples of Trump family business maneuverings that Democrats say can be tied to government policies.
Trump’s opponents are confident that he will not prevail in the most extreme version of his secrecy claims. But they also acknowledge that the process for litigating those questions is a slow one that can drag out beyond January 20, 2029, when he leaves office.
Democrats on the Hill are watching the Trump administration’s legal arguments closely, as they plot the various of tools they’ll have at their disposal to fight back — including pressure points that go beyond pressing for compliance in court.
“There are the collateral consequences of being held in contempt, of refusing to provide documents, and standing behind a blatantly unlawful assertions of executive privilege,” a senior House aide, who spoke on the condition of not being named so they could talk openly about Democrats’ thinking, told CNN.
Democrats believe that the threat of pushback from the public, investors, state authorities and future administrations will encourage business leaders and others targeted with subpoenas to participate in oversight probes, even if Trump is claiming privilege could shield them.
“The private sector folks are going to be completely caught in the middle of this,” Bair, who did congressional oversight work for the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said. He predicted that lawmakers “are going to make it as painful as possible” for any company that doesn’t hand documents sought by Congress.
“They will say your name on television as many times as possible until the public pressure builds up enough for compliance,” Bair said.
The president’s position on executive privilege for outside advisers could soon be tested in a Justice Department effort to block a subpoena to Boris Epshteyn – a legal adviser for Trump who does not work in the government – in a case brought by the American Bar Association to challenge the administration’s pressure campaign on law firms.
In a letter to the White House this week, Senate Democrats led by California Sen. Adam Schiff demanded the White House inform them which other non-government advisers if believes the presidential privilege covers.
Executive privilege, they wrote, “is not an unlimited shield designed to insulate private citizens, informal advisers, and non-governmental actors from congressional oversight and public accountability.”

items.body_text:
Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

Once bitter enemies Amhara, Tigray reach understandings in fight against Ethiopian govt          
        In mid-August, the leader of the Amhara insurgency fighting to overthrow Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed made a surprising announcement.
The collection of armed Amhara movements fighting in the country’s northwest under the unified Fano umbrella would join an alliance of seven other anti-government groups across the country, Fano leader Zemene Kassie told the Swiss publication, Le Temps.
What makes the move surprising is that the alliance includes members of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), whom the Amhara forces that make up the Fano fought against during the 2020-2022 war.
In addition to the TPLF, the alliance includes forces from Gumuz, Oromo, the Berta people and Somalia, Zemene said.
At the national level, the fight between Ethiopian oppositional groups and the government comes against the backdrop of a struggle over the future of the country’s multinational federal system and state’s right to self-determination.
However, this tension has a larger regional dynamic given Ethiopia’s involvement in the war in Sudan and its expressed desire to secure access to the Red Sea either by diplomatic coup or by force.
While fighting between the Fano and the Ethiopian government has transformed much of the Amhara Region into an active war zone since late 2023, the beginning of August saw clashes between TPLF forces and the Ethiopian military that threatened to transform long standing simmering tensions between the groups into an active war.
An African Union diplomat based in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr at the time that any expansion of the fighting in Tigray would have an impact on the calculations of every regional actor because the borders linking Sudan, Ethiopia and Eritrea are no longer merely dividing lines between states. They now form part of an interconnected regional security system in which domestic wars and geopolitical interests overlap, the diplomat added, making any new outbreak of fighting in Tigray a potential factor in reshaping the security landscape of the entire East African region.
The government has responded to the early August clashes with increased military activity.
In a statement issued on Friday, the Tigray regional government warned the international community that the region is nearing “another catastrophic war.”
An economic and security blockade has escalated following clashes that broke out on August 1, the statement added, with air strikes and artillery shelling hitting civilian areas, causing casualties and destruction and disrupting cultural activities.
In an interview with Oromia Broadcasting Network on August 7, Abiy criticized the TPLF leadership, accusing it of clinging to outdated political methods and forging alliances that he said threaten stability.
TPLF deputy chair Amanuel Assefa pointed to a strike on August 20, when a drone hit a residential area in Mekelle, Tigray’s capital. Residents speaking to Mada Masr confirmed the strike and said several homes were damaged.
Medical sources at Mekelle’s Ayder Specialized Hospital said 13 people were brought in with injuries following the strike, including five women and children, with three in serious condition. The injured ranged in age from two to 60, the sources said.
Tigrayan authorities also said a second strike hit near Mekelle University, though there is no confirmed information on casualties or damage as of the time of publishing.
The strike on Mekelle came only days after another attack that Tigrayan authorities attributed to the Ethiopian military, where a drone struck a farmers’ training center in the Dandera village, about 15 km from Mekelle, on August 18.
While the government hit Tigray, Fano forces continued to secure strategic wins against the Ethiopian military.
Fano forces in the Wollo provinces of Amhara – which borders southern Tigray — have claimed significant military victories in the past week along the Raya
