items.body_text:
Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
Prague Morning
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.
Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.
At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.
The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.
The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.
The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.
How the Champions League league phase works
The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.
Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.
The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.
The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

items.body_text:
Police Arrest Foreign National on Allegations of Abandoning Abkhaz Blogger Daur Buava in Danger
The Georgian Interior Ministry announced the arrest of a foreign national in connection with Abkhaz blogger Daur Buava’s death, noting the accused abandoned Buava in “critical and life-threatening condition” after the two took a narcotic substance in a Tbilisi apartment. The Ministry did not disclose the name or the nationality of the accused.
According to the Ministry, the investigation shows that Buava and the suspect, who were friends, “were together at Daur Buava’s temporary residence in Tbilisi, Didi Dighomi, where they used a narcotic substance, after which both of them became unwell.” The Ministry said that questioning established that the suspect left Buava, who was “in a critical and life-threatening condition,” alone.
“Specifically, the accused locked the door of the apartment from the outside using a second key and left the scene without informing anyone about what had happened or approaching anyone to seek help for Daur Buava,” the Ministry said.
According to the Ministry’s statement, an investigation is underway under Articles 115 and 128 of the Criminal Code, covering incitement to suicide [a standard provision when a person is found dead in unclear circumstances in Georgia], and abandoning a person in danger.
On August 28, reports emerged that Buava, a 31-year-old Abkhaz blogger and TikToker who lived in Tbilisi-controlled territory and published videos promoting Abkhaz-Georgian friendship, was found dead in Tbilisi.
His body was reportedly discovered in a Tbilisi apartment on August 27, days after his suspected death, after neighbors raised concerns over a strong odor. The Interior Ministry said a preliminary inspection of the body found no signs of violence.
Buava, known on TikTok as Tarielovich and followed by more than 100,000 people, was born in Tkvarcheli, occupied Abkhazia, and moved to Georgia proper in 2021, where he was granted Georgian citizenship under a simplified procedure in 2022. He lived in Tbilisi-controlled territory and published videos promoting Abkhaz-Georgian friendship.
In 2022, the de facto security service of Sokhumi filed charges of high treason against Buava, saying the blogger published videos with “direct and latent appeals to an unlimited circle of users aimed at damaging sovereignty, territorial integrity, national security and defense capacity.”

Orchards, Roads Damaged as Rains Cause Flooding in Imereti
Heavy rains on August 27 damaged orchards, crops, and roads in the western Georgian region of Imereti, with the damage particularly affecting neighborhoods and villages in Baghdati Municipality.
Videos from the scene show streams of water rushing through roads and orchards and entering homes, with locals saying the rains caused small rivers to swell suddenly. Residents are seen struggling to protect their houses, yards and belongings, while appealing to the authorities for assistance.
“In just half an hour, this small river wreaked havoc on all my family’s work,” a resident of Obcha village of Baghdati municipality wrote on social media, posting videos of the orchard filled by rapidly moving water and a flooded house. “I have no words. I walk around in tears.”
Local media also published an image showing a section of a forest-covered slope that had collapsed.
Heavy flooding was also reported in villages in nearby Zestaphoni Municipality, while rainwater flooded streets in Kutaisi, the region’s administrative center.
The Baghdati Municipality City Hall said authorities are operating in emergency mode, and a commission has been set up to assess the damage. Hundreds of households have been left without gas and electricity.

items.title: Asbestos allegedly found under Rustaveli Avenue during renovation
items.summary: The Public Defender’s Office has urged the authorities to verify the reports.
items.body_text:
Georgia’s Public Defender’s Office has issued a warning, calling on Tbilisi City Hall to investigate the presence of asbestos allegedly found under Rustaveli Avenue during ongoing rehabilitation work.
The agency issued its appeal after pictures of what appears to be asbestos found on Rustaveli Avenue surfaced online on 21 August. Social media user Irakli Pipia said that asbestos was used by the Soviet authorities to construct water pipes under the thoroughfare.
On Thursday, urban and environmental activist Nata Peradze said that samples of the shattered asbestos pipes were collected and are ready to be sent to a laboratory in Berlin. She added that they need to raise funds for the analysis.
The Public Defender of Georgia issued its appeal on Facebook on Thursday.
‘Asbestos is a substance with high health risk and its exposure is related to serious diseases, including mesothelioma and lung cancer. The risk increases sharply during mechanical exposure, cutting, crushing, drilling and removal from the ground.’
‘International standards for asbestos regulation have not been fully implemented in Georgia, technical regulations have not been adopted that would regulate the protection of employees from exposure to asbestos in the workplace’, the agency said.
It also warned that schools located around the avenue will start their classes on 15 September, and that students could potentially be exposed to asbestos.
‘Children are a particularly vulnerable group to asbestos exposure, as their respiratory system is still in the process of formation, and the latent period of asbestos-related diseases lasts for decades.’
The Public Defender called on Tbilisi City hall to determine whether the material found in the renovation area contains asbestos, and to spread awareness about the matter.
In 2019, more than 70,000 people in the EU died from past exposure to asbestos at work.
Authorities have been discussing the renovation of Rustaveli Avenue since 2023. The renovation started in late July, 2026 with authorities saying it is scheduled to be finished in November.
The construction company responsible for the rehabilitation work has been fined four times for failing to adhere to the stipulated work schedule, leading to a total of ₾5,000 ($1,900) in fines.
Rustaveli Avenue has historically been the site of numerous mass protests and clashes between protesters and riot police.

items.title: Lavrov says Armenia must choose between EU and EAEU
items.summary: Lavrov also criticised Yerevan for its handling of Russia’s concession over Armenia’s railways.
items.body_text:
Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said Armenia must choose between the EU and its membership in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), echoing previous remarks issued by other Russian officials.
Lavrov’s remarks reflect the deepening standoff between the two countries. Armenia pushes towards EU integration, which Russia sees as incompatible with EAEU membership. Pashinyan also wants to restructure the ownership of the Russia-run national railway over concerns about deterring foreign investments. Those two issues together highlight Armenia’s effort to balance its relationship with historical partner Russia while pivoting towards the West.
On Armenia’s EU aspirations, Lavrov said that Pashinyan’s position, that a referendum on EU membership can only be discussed after Armenia submits its application and drafts a ‘road map’, shows that he does not fully ‘trust his own people’ to make an honest choice. Lavrov recalled that in May, EAEU countries called on Armenia to hold a referendum to decide whether to stay with the EAEU or join the EU, which he said is a justified request.
‘The norms of one organisation are incompatible with the norms of the other organisation. This has been said many times’, Lavrov said.
Lavrov argued that Armenia now has to choose between the EU and what it already has, pointing to trade turnover which he said exceeded $6 billion in the past three years and had reached $12 billion in one year. He did not specify whether he meant trade between Armenia and the EAEU or with Russia.
Turning to the railway issue, Lavrov stressed that Russia has done everything for its part to normalise relations with Armenia, and expressed surprise that Armenia discusses the railway concession publicly rather than directly with its partner.
Armenia’s railway system is owned by Russian Railways (RZhD) under a 30-year concession signed in 2008.
Earlier in August, Pashinyan told reporters that Armenia is seeking to negotiate a compromise with Russia over the Russian-run national railway, rather than unilaterally cancelling Russian Railways’ (RZhD) management contract. Pashinyan first called for ending the RZhD’s presence in February, arguing that Russian control discourages investment from international partners. In July, he threatened arbitration and a $2 billion annual bill for RZhD’s management rights, triggering warnings from Russia.
The Russian Foreign Ministry, in response, has accused the West of ‘blackmailing’ Armenia over the concession of the railway.
‘They demand the removal of the “Russian factor” from the transport sector, while in return promising multimillion-dollar investments and access to projects whose economic viability is hardly apparent’, the Russian ministry said.
During a press briefing on Thursday, Pashinyan said Armenia expressed its positions on Russia and its security bloc, the Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO), ‘in a transparent, public, and honest manner’.
Armenia’s membership in the CSTO has also been called into question by Russia. Yerevan ‘froze’ its membership in the bloc in early 2024, with Pashinyan on Monday saying resuming Armenia’s membership in the CSTO was not in his government’s five-year plan.
‘I would be very happy if the organisation decided to expel Armenia from the CSTO. It would free us from the dilemma of whether or not to withdraw’, he said at the time.

items.title: Azerbaijan calls on Russia to investigate protest in front of its embassy in Moscow
items.summary: Baku described the protest as an ‘ugly and biased campaign’ against Azerbaijan.
items.body_text:
Azerbaijan has called on Russia to investigate three National Bolsheviks for putting up banners on the walls of the Azerbaijani Embassy in Moscow calling for the release of Russians detained in Azerbaijan. Baku has called the incident an ‘unacceptable provocation’.
Footage from the small protest appeared on a Telegram channel linked to the National Bolshevik Movement. In the video, the protesters criticised Azerbaijan for launching criminal cases against Russians.
Their banners read: ‘Azerbaijan’s State Security Service tortures, [Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev] covers it up!, ‘Russian blood is on your hands!’, and ‘Let the Russian citizens go!’.
The movement said that Azerbaijan ‘consistently pursues an anti-Russian policy’.
A few hours later Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry issued an official statement saying that the incident might be aimed ‘at artificially straining Azerbaijani-Russian relations’.
The ministry described the protest as an ‘ugly and biased campaign’ against Azerbaijan, which it claimed was being waged in certain Russian media outlets.
On 19 August, Azerbaijan Prosecutor General’s Office issued warrants for three Russian citizens accusing them of making calls to overthrow the government.
Relations between Azerbaijan and Russia deteriorated following the crash of an Azerbaijan Airlines passenger plane shot down in Grozny in December 2024, which resulted in the deaths of 38 people.
Russia subsequently arrested Azerbaijanis, accusing them of crimes committed as far back as the early 2000s; Azerbaijan characterized these actions as an instance of ethnic discrimination.
The arrests of Azerbaijanis in Russia were followed by the arrests of Russian citizens in Azerbaijan in June.

items.body_text:
Finnish politicians are reacting to the passing of the Norwegian king, Harald V, who died on Friday.
His successor, Crown Prince Haakon, immediately ascended the throne.
Norway's government on Friday declared a period of national mourning, which will continue until the king's funeral.
President Alexander Stubb expressed his condolences on the death of Harald in a post on X.
European Parliament member Anna-Maja Henriksson meanwhile said she shares the grief of the Norwegian people and the royal family.
President Niinistö pays warm tribute
Former Finnish President Sauli Niinistö described the late King Harald of Norway as a wise leader.
"He was not only a king but also a very good-humoured person," Niinistö told Yle in an interview.
Niinistö said the king was a "wise elder" who knew how to make his views count.
"He was very easy to talk to about a wide range of subjects, and he also used a lot of humour."
Harald had a very positive view of Finland, and Nordic cooperation was important to him. Their conversations sometimes touched on historical events as well.
Niinistö and King Harald met around ten times over the years at international gatherings.
"King Harald lived for his nation and its success. And now that nation carries on," Niinistö said.

items.title: Europe's monarchs and world leaders mourn Norway's King Harald
items.summary: European monarchs and world leaders paid to Norway's King Harald, after the royal palace announced his death aged 89.
items.body_text:
Harald was the continent's oldest reigning monarch. His son Haakon automatically succeeded him to the throne.
Here are some of the main tributes:
Britain's King Charles
Britain's King Charles III hailed "dear cousin", who he said had served "with unwavering dedication, guiding Norway through times of great change with warmth and humility".
"As Norway mourns the loss of so towering a figure, my whole family join in remembering a much-loved kinsman and friend whose kindness, compassion and deep sense of duty echoed from across the sea and across the decades," the king said in a statement, personally signed Charles R.
Danish and Swedish monarchs
The kings of Denmark and Sweden called Harald an "extraordinary" leader and good friend who unified his country.
"Both as head of state and a successful athlete, he was an outstanding representative of his country. He gave 'All for Norway'," Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf said, referring to Harald's royal motto.
Denmark's King Frederik X said the late monarch was "an extraordinary man" who "joined duty and responsibility with presence and compassion".
Swiss president
The Swiss president Guy Parmelin wrote on X that Harald "will be remembered for his steadfast leadership and devoted service to his country".
Dutch royal family
The Dutch royal family recalled "unforgettable" journeys with King Harald around Oslo and the rest of Norway. "We cherish the memory of our special friendship with him in our hearts. King Harald served his country with love, pride, and conviction," said the family in a statement.
Belgian royals
Harald's "humour, humanity and sincerity made him a truly special man", Belgium's King Philippe and Queen Mathilde said.
"Generations of Norwegians grew up with him. For decades, he was a familiar and reassuring presence, a beacon of stability for his country. He fulfilled his role with unwavering dedication, loyalty and dignity," they said in a statement.
Italy PM
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, in a post on X, called Harald: "A monarch who served his nation with equanimity, authority and a deep sense of institutional duty, helping to strengthen the ties between Norway and Italy throughout his long reign."
Spain's royal family
Spain's royal family hailed King Harald as an "example of responsibility, dignity, simplicity, and tireless dedication to the service" of his country.
"With respect and admiration for him, as well as deep sadness, we offer our condolences" on the king's death, they wrote on social media.
Jordan's royal family
Jordan's Royal Hashemite Court said it mourned the passing of King Harald "may his soul rest in peace".
The court "expresses the deepest sympathies of His Majesty and the Jordanian people, as they stand with Norway and its people at this difficult time".
King Abdullah ordered his court to observe three days of mourning, a statement from the court added.
UN chief
A spokesman for UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply saddened" by the king's death.
"He will be remembered for his engagement for children's welfare and environmental issues, his support for diversity and calls for generosity," the statement added.
NATO, EU chiefs
Harald "showed himself to be a dedicated leader," posted Mark Rutte, head of the NATO alliance that includes Norway.
"His own military roots made him a champion of the Norwegian military and a long-time friend of NATO," he wrote online.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that Harald "served his country with warmth, humility and an unwavering sense of duty".
French president
Harald "worked tirelessly throughout his reign to strengthen the ties uniting Norway and France", Emmanuel Macron wrote on X, recalling a "warm welcome" on his visit to Oslo in June 2025.
Ukraine's President
"His Majesty embodied dignity, wisdom, and an unwavering commitment to his country," said Volodymyr Zelensky in a statement.

items.title: Iceland votes on whether to resume EU membership talks
items.summary: Icelanders began voting Saturday in a referendum on whether to resume membership negotiations with the European Union, in a tight race that will be closely watched in Brussels.
items.body_text:
The country of just under 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of a 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy.
The membership talks were suspended in 2013 when a eurosceptic government came to power.
The referendum result is expected to go down to the wire, with the latest Gallup poll crediting the 'No' camp with 51.6 percent of voter support and the 'Yes' side with 48.4 percent, a gap within the statistical margin of error.
READ ALSO: As Iceland votes on the EU, which countries could be next to join?
"It's pretty tight, but I'm always optimistic," Foreign Minister Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir, a staunch europhile, told AFP ahead of the vote. "It's not done until it's done."
Voting began at 9:00 am (0900 GMT) and closes at 10:00 pm. With no exit polls and given the tight race, the first reliable results are only expected late Saturday at the earliest.
The around 273,000 voters are being asked to answer 'Yes' or 'No' to the question: "Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?"
If the 'Yes' side wins, an accession agreement would be negotiated with Brussels and then put to a new referendum on actual membership.
The issue of fisheries -- a pillar of Iceland's economy and over which Reykjavik wants to retain exclusive control -- would have to be hammered out with Brussels, which this time around appears more willing to compromise.
"The fundaments (of the debate) are very domestic, but there is a significant impact that has come with the second term of (US President) Donald Trump and this sort of geopolitical upheaval," Bifrost University political scientist Eirikur Bergmann told AFP.
With Iceland's economy now flourishing, some voters see no reason to discuss EU membership, since the country already has access to the single market as a member of the European Economic Area.
"It's like if you are in a relationship with someone you don't live with, and if you lose something you have by getting married, then why get married?" said Hjordis Vilhjalmsdottir, a 60-year-old radio presenter wearing glasses in the red, blue and white of Iceland's flag.
"We don't need Brussels to rule us. We can do it ourselves," said Elias Theodorsson, a 65-year-old entrepreneur.
"We used to be one of the poorest countries in Europe only a hundred years ago. And now we are the most prominent country in Europe. We did it ourselves," he said.
Money talks
The flip side of Iceland's regained prosperity is soaring inflation and interest rates.
Some households are paying nine percent interest on their mortgages, making the prospect of joining the eurozone -- with its much lower rates -- very appealing.
"There's such a big gap, and it would mean so much for my household," said Alexandra Yr van Erven, a 32-year-old university administrator.
"I just think it's the responsible thing to do, to give this government the agency to negotiate a deal with the EU, so we can see what the possibilities are. And then we can evaluate the deal."
On the global stage, the return of war in Europe with Russia's invasion of Ukraine has shaken established security doctrines.
Trump's unpredictability and his threats to take over neighbouring Greenland -- which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions -- have added to Icelanders' concerns.
Their island is strategically located in the sub-Arctic, has no military and depends on NATO and a 1951 bilateral agreement with the United States for its defence.
"People are now bringing into question the validity of that agreement," Bergmann said. "The geopolitical shifts are impacting the debate, but they're not driving it."
The referendum result will be followed closely by the EU, which has not welcomed a wealthy, net contributor to its budget since 1995.
Brussels would see Icelandic membership as an example of positive enlargement that could also make it more palatable for member states to agree to take in poorer countries like Montenegro -- or even help change some minds in ultra-wealth

items.title: Inside Sweden: Why Swedes should get over the awkwardness and chat to strangers
items.summary: The Local's Emma Löfgren was left feeling all warm and fuzzy after a trip abroad, and wonders if her fellow Swedes have something to learn. Plus: Our top stories of the week.
items.body_text:
Hej,
I lived and worked in Scotland for many years before moving back to Sweden, dragging my now-husband along with me. When we left in 2015, we said we would try to go back once a year – but then the pandemic happened, children happened, and you know how it goes.
But this summer we got a chance to finally go back for the first time in years, to spend a week in the East Neuk of Fife, the place in Scotland where I still feel the most at home, despite also having stayed for quite a bit of time in the Western Isles and Aberdeen.
With its fishing villages, art communities, strong focus on local produce, and relatively elderly population, it's probably as close to the part of Sweden I live in today (Österlen) as you get.
But there are still some things that are very different.
On our way from the airport, walking down the aisle of a busy train from Edinburgh and finding only single seats, it didn't take long for a man (with crutches!) to get up to offer me his, so my daughters and I could sit together. Just a bit later, someone immediately got up without hesitation to help my husband drag our three heavy suitcases off the bus.
It's not that you never get helped in Sweden (and I often talk about how Swedes are much more friendly and helpful than our reserved reputation suggests – you just have to ask before we step into your personal zone), but you feel more welcome when it's spontaneously offered, without a pause to see if anyone else in the vicinity is going to make the first move.
The next morning I got pulled into conversation with a couple from another part of Scotland, who had just wrapped up their holiday and were about to head home. I spent an hour on an ill-advised day trip to Edinburgh chatting with a grandmother about life, work and grandchildren. An artist whose studio we visited overheard our family's mix of Swedish, Italian and English and curiously asked what languages we were speaking, sparking another conversation.
It didn't happen on this visit, but I fondly remember one train ride during the Five Nations rugby tournament when I was randomly offered champagne by the family next to me who were celebrating Scotland's win over… someone (I don't follow rugby myself).
My four-year-old who doesn't speak English quickly learned to communicate with the Fife grannies, gesticulating wildly when they admired her colourful nails to show that it was her mummy who had painted them. She also figured out that "how old are you" tended to be one of the standard questions, so she'd gregariously point at herself to say "four" and her sister to say "one". And of course the most important words in the English language: "Chocolate ice cream". Very handy to be able to bypass your parents (we're still working on "please").
There are a great many things I appreciate about Sweden. Not feeling like I'm defying death every time I get on a bus is one of them ("Where are the seatbelts," my daughter enquired). I don't need the kind of action in my life where the driver is reversing around the corner of a narrow street at way too many miles per hour, because you happened to come face to face with a tractor.
But a week of chatting with strangers left me feeling happier and warmer on the inside than I had in a long time. Again, it's not that it never happens in Sweden, and I find my part of the country pretty friendly, but it doesn't happen this often or this enthusiastically.
Now, I'm an introvert even as Swedes go. I like my privacy and being left alone. But human interaction is part of the glue that holds society together, and I can't help thinking we could use more of these random, friendly encounters with strangers in Sweden.
For one thing, it could reduce loneliness and build stronger communities. It also challenges the fear of awkwardness and "The Other" – while equal rights for groups and individuals are important in Sweden, unspoken social norms about what one does and doesn't are strong, and there's a tendency to punish those who step outs

items.title: Berlin being 'blackmailed' after cyberattack
items.summary: Berlin's mayor on Friday said the city was being blackmailed after a data theft during a cyberattack two weeks ago.
items.body_text:
According to the German weekly Der Spiegel, the blackmailers are demanding 30 bitcoins -- the equivalent of about €2 million or $2.5 million.
The publication, which cited confirmation from a security source, added that the group involved is believed to be the hacker collective Rhysida.
Rhysida notably claimed responsibility for a ransomware attack against the British Library in 2023 and demanded payment of 20 bitcoins -- worth some $850,000 at the time.
"Berlin is the victim of a serious crime," said Kai Wegner, the outgoing mayor of the capital, which is both a city and a regional state.
"The demand came in early on Thursday evening. Berlin will not give in to blackmail."
The cyberattack on August 14 left several city administrations, especially those dealing with housing and the environment, cut off from the network for a week.
All applications for housing benefits and payments were impossible for several days.
The authorities initially claimed that no sensitive data had been stolen but on Wednesday admitted that personal data may have been affected.
According to Der Spiegel, Rhysida was threatening to publish the data if it did not receive the money within a week.
Germany's security services are working flat-out to apprehend the perpetrators, Wegner said, without naming them.
Checks were also being made about which data was stolen.
In the British Library case, it refused to pay the ransom and Rhysida published about 500,000 files on the dark web containing the personal data of visitors, subscribers and staff.
One of Berlin's deputy mayors, Iris Spranger, said the cyberattack did not affect the holding of elections in the city-state on September 20.
"The vote is 100 percent secure," she added.

"It's like if you are in a relationship with someone you don't live with, and if you lose something you have by getting married, then why get married?" said Hjordis Vilhjalmsdottir, a 60-year-old radio presenter wearing glasses in the red, blue and white of Iceland's flag.
"We don't need Brussels to rule us. We can do it ourselves," said Elias Theodorsson, a 65-year-old entrepreneur.
"We used to be one of the poorest countries in Europe only a hundred years ago. And now we are the most prominent country in Europe. We did it ourselves," he said.
Money talks
The flip side of Iceland's regained prosperity is soaring inflation and interest rates.
Some households are paying nine percent interest on their mortgages, making the prospect of joining the eurozone -- with its much lower rates -- very appealing.
"There's such a big gap, and it would mean so much for my household," said Alexandra Yr van Erven, a 32-year-old university administrator.
"I just think it's the responsible thing to do, to give this government the agency to negotiate a deal with the EU, so we can see what the possibilities are. And then we can evaluate the deal."
On the global stage, the return of war in Europe with Russia's invasion of Ukraine has shaken established security doctrines.
Trump's unpredictability and his threats to take over neighbouring Greenland -- which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions -- have added to Icelanders' concerns.
Their island is strategically located in the sub-Arctic, has no military and depends on NATO and a 1951 bilateral agreement with the United States for its defence.
"People are now bringing into question the validity of that agreement," Bergmann said. "The geopolitical shifts are impacting the debate, but they're not driving it."
The referendum result will be followed closely by the EU, which has not welcomed a wealthy, net contributor to its budget since 1995.
Brussels would see Icelandic membership as an example of positive enlargement that could also make it more palatable for member states to agree to take in poorer countries like Montenegro -- or even help change some minds in ultra-wealth

items.title: Inside Germany: The fascist urge to attack Bauhaus and the 'real' city of love
items.summary: From the AfD's plan to defund one of Germany's most successful cultural exports, to the claim that Berlin is Europe's true capital of love, Inside Germany is our weekly look at some of the recent news and talking points you may have missed.
items.body_text:
What do a dome desk lamp, a fitted modular kitchen, Sans-Serif typography and an Apple computer mouse have in common?
The design for each of them can be traced back to Germany’s Bauhaus movement, which revolutionised architecture and product design with an emphasis on minimalist utility.
Widely considered to be among the most influential art movements of the modern era, Bauhaus is unparalleled in terms of its global reach, longevity and the impact it's had on so many of the sleek and “modern” looking objects in our everyday lives. And it’s definitively German in origin.
So why does the Alternative for Germany (AfD) want to shut it down?
Within the far-right party’s 150 page election manifesto for Saxony-Anhalt is a – shall we say interesting? – section which accuses the state government of "running an image campaign called '#modern thinking' that seeks to derive the identity of Saxony-Anhalt from Bauhaus."
The AfD would rather shift Germany’s public identity away from internationalist, or "rootless", modernism. The party wants to cut budgets for institutions promoting modern, avant-garde and progressive art, and redirect tax dollars toward what it sees as more 'traditionally German' culture.
This is not the first time that the AfD has targeted Bauhaus, and notably not the first time that Bauhaus has been targeted by fascist politics.
In fact, many have commented on the fact that the AfD’s criticism of Bauhaus sounds quite similar to that of the Nazis – who also rejected the liberal and cosmopolitan aspects of the movement and wanted to promote more 'traditional' German art and literature.
The Nazis shut down the Bauhaus school in Berlin in 1933, and many of the artists most prominently associated with the movement fled Germany to avoid persecution.
Today the Bauhaus campus and museum in Dessau are a significant attraction within a region that has suffered from de-industrialisation for years. If the AfD were to take power in the state, perhaps this too would be lost.
As of Friday, just over a week from Saxony-Anhalt’s election, polls showed the AfD having the support of 40 percent of voters in the state. However, according to the latest calculations, this would not be enough for the party to automatically take power as a single-party government.
READ ALSO: Who can vote in Germany's high-stakes state elections this September?
What is this?
Unless you've been close to the front lines of the war in Ukraine, or followed the news from there quite closely, you might not immediately recognise what's going on in the above photo, which was taken at a demonstration in Berlin earlier this week.
The net seen above is similar to that used over roads and bases in Ukraine, designed to block explosive drones.
In parts of Ukraine, whole towns are covered in anti-drone nets to prevent attacks by FPV drones that explode on impact. Surprisingly, a bit of mesh netting is enough to prevent fatalities and structural damage in many cases.
The above scene was set up by activists as part of an installation on August 24th to mark Ukrainian independence day and call attention to Russian drone attacks. On the same day, Ukraine's allies pledged to keep up their support amid Russia's escalating attacks.
Germany is Ukraine's biggest military backer, having overtaken the US about a year ago after President Donald Trump dialled back military deliveries.
Is Berlin the real city of love?
Sorry Paris, Europe’s real city of love is on the Spree – at least according to Berlin’s public transit company Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe (BVG).
Reliability on the U-Bahn may be hit or miss, but when it comes to marketing BVG consistently delivers.
The latest example being a short video which makes a pretty compelling argument for Berlin being the true capital of love – in all of its weird, wild and dirty forms.

items.title: Gov't pledges more resilient tourism in Labuan Bajo post-earthquake
items.summary: The Indonesian Tourism Ministry has committed to ensuring that Labuan Bajo will not merely recover from a recent ...
items.body_text:
To achieve this, the ministry will strengthen disaster risk management and develop new land-based tourist attractions in West Manggarai District, East Nusa Tenggara.
“We want tourism to continue to grow, underpinned by enhanced safety and broader economic benefits for the local community,” Tourism Minister Widiyanti Putri Wardhana said in a statement released here on Saturday.
On Friday (August 28), Minister Wardhana held a coordination meeting with the West Manggarai regional administration, industry players, and tourism associations in Labuan Bajo.
The meeting focused on recovery strategies for the region’s tourism sector following the August 15 quake, while also addressing Labuan Bajo’s broader development.
These measures are being prioritized based on the severity of damage, the operational readiness of tourism destinations, and the restoration of local livelihoods.
The recovery efforts will cover the entire tourism supply chain, including hotels, restaurants, tourism villages, tour boats, tour guides, as well as local micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Beyond restoring the local economy and rebuilding market confidence, the efforts aim to strengthen standard operating procedures (SOPs) for emergency response, evacuation routes, and on-site crisis communication systems.
Head of West Manggarai District Edistasius Endi noted that tourism activities have been operating safely and normally since the earthquake. The district has recorded 2,854 boat departures and 32,692 tourist trips post-disaster.
Domestic and international flight traffic also remains stable. Komodo National Park and Padar Island have reopened to the public after passing rigorous safety assessments.
To sustain this positive trend, the Tourism Ministry will enhance marine tourism safety competencies through the Indonesian Tourism Workforce Certification (SATRIA) program. Simultaneously, the government will expand the development of land-based destinations, including Kukusan Island, Kelor Island, and Rangko Cave.

items.title: Lampung Police urge parents to monitor children's social circle, media
items.summary: The Lampung Regional Police have urged parents to step up supervision of their children's daily activities, social ...
items.body_text:
"Such supervision is crucial to prevent children from becoming involved in various issues, ranging from drug abuse, promiscuity, and illegal online loans, to activities that could turn violent," Lampung Regional Police spokeswoman Senior Commissioner Yuni Iswandari said on Saturday.
Iswandari stressed that merely knowing a child's whereabouts is insufficient; parents must also actively monitor their social environment and digital footprint to prevent them from engaging in destructive behaviors that could jeopardize their futures.
Rapid technological advancements necessitate active parental monitoring in the digital space. Illegal online lending platforms are a primary concern, prompting her to call on parents to educate their children about the dangers of deceptive online offers.
"Children and teenagers who do not fully grasp the risks of debt can easily be tempted by loan offers or illegal financial activities on the internet," she warned.
Furthermore, Iswandari cautioned parents against allowing minors to participate in public rallies that could escalate into riots.
"We appeal to parents to ensure their children steer clear of potentially chaotic rallies. They might just be following the crowd, but they could easily end up as victims if the situation becomes volatile," she explained.
She pointed out that adolescents are highly susceptible to peer pressure, making open communication at home essential to equip them with the confidence to refuse risky invitations.
"Establish open communication so that children do not solely turn to their peers or social media for answers. Help them distinguish between positive activities and those that could endanger them," Iswandari advised.
Reiterating that early prevention is vital, she urged parents to stay vigilant regarding any sudden changes in their children's behavior, social circles, or daily routines.
"Do not let a child's future be compromised by a momentary poor decision or peer pressure. We must take preventive measures early on so they do not fall prey to drugs, promiscuity, illegal loans, or chaotic riots," she concluded.

items.title: Indonesia pushes for safer, evidence-based stem cell therapy
items.summary: The Health Ministry's Director of Referral Health Service Development, Yanti Herman, has encouraged the development ...
items.body_text:
Stem cell therapy is not a service that can be provided without strong clinical governance and oversight,
At the "Update on Stem Cell Therapy and Its Derivatives in Indonesia" event here on Saturday, Herman's remarks were read out by Sri Nuraini, Head of the Regenerative Therapy and Medical Innovation Working Group.
"Stem cell therapy and its derivative products, such as secretome, exosomes, and extracellular vesicles, offer hope for patients with various diseases that were previously difficult to treat, including in orthopedics, aesthetics, neurology, and other fields," Herman said in her statement.
She added that the Health Ministry emphasized three key points in the discussion, including the need for the public to have accurate information about stem cell-based therapies, including their proven benefits, appropriate indications, potential risks, and limitations.
"Public education is very important so that people can distinguish between promising innovations and therapy claims that are not yet supported by adequate scientific evidence," she said.
In addition, such therapies must be administered by competent medical personnel using products that meet established requirements and are produced by licensed stem cell processing laboratories, with traceable services and proper monitoring.
"Stem cell therapy is not a service that can be provided without strong clinical governance and oversight," she said.
The Health Ministry also called for the strengthening of the regenerative therapy ecosystem, particularly stem cell therapy, through regulatory development, research hospitals, expanded laboratory capacity, and stronger systems for recording and monitoring patient outcomes.
According to Herman, the goal of developing stem cell therapy is not merely to introduce new technology but to ensure that it can be translated into safe, high-quality, evidence-based services that provide real benefits to patients.
Stem cell services cover a series of medical procedures, from the collection, storage, and processing of cells to the administration of therapy from donor to recipient. Such therapies may be autologous, using the patient's own cells, or allogeneic, using cells from public donors, and must meet quality, safety, and efficacy standards.

items.title: Di Tengah Friksi PB PTMSI dan IPL, Nasib Atlet Tenis Meja Ikut Terdampak
items.summary: Friksi antara PB PTMSI dan IPL tidak lagi sebatas perebutan ruang organisasi, tetapi berpotensi memengaruhi kesempatan atlet mengikuti kompetisi
items.body_text:
Di Tengah Friksi PB PTMSI dan IPL, Nasib Atlet Tenis Meja Ikut Terdampak
Friksi antara PB PTMSI dan IPL tidak lagi sebatas perebutan ruang organisasi, tetapi berpotensi memengaruhi kesempatan atlet mengikuti kompetisi
PB PTMSI Ancam Tak Beri Rekomendasi, Atlet IPL Terancam Kehilangan Akses Kompetisi
TRIBUNNEWS.COM — Friksi keorganisasian olahraga tenis meja Indonesia kembali mencuat dan mulai bersentuhan langsung dengan kepentingan atlet.
Persoalan antara Pengurus Besar Persatuan Tenis Meja Seluruh Indonesia (PB PTMSI) dan Indonesia Pingpong League (IPL) tidak lagi sebatas perebutan ruang organisasi, tetapi berpotensi memengaruhi kesempatan atlet mengikuti kompetisi dan jalur pembinaan prestasi.
Baca juga: Peter Layardi Beberkan Program Unggulan PB PTMSI Usai Resmi Dilantik KONI Pusat
Persoalan itu terlihat dari sikap PB PTMSI terhadap atlet yang mengikuti kompetisi IPL.
Di tengah belum tuntasnya tarik-menarik pengakuan organisasi antara PB PTMSI dan IPL, para atlet berada pada posisi yang rentan: mengikuti kompetisi dapat membuka peluang bertanding dan mengasah prestasi, tetapi sekaligus berisiko memengaruhi akses mereka terhadap agenda yang berada di bawah PB PTMSI.
Situasi tersebut kembali terlihat ketika IPL menggelar Grand Final Season 2 di Trans Studio Mall Cibubur pada 26–30 Agustus 2026.
PB PTMSI Klaim Tak Dilibatkan
PB PTMSI menyatakan tidak mengetahui adanya permintaan izin maupun pemberitahuan dari IPL terkait penyelenggaraan kompetisi tersebut.
Ketua Umum PB PTMSI, Peter Layardi Lay mengatakan IPL juga tidak mengajukan kerja sama dengan organisasinya sebelum kompetisi berlangsung.
“Mereka (IPL) juga tidak mengajukan pemberitahuan ataupun melakukan kerja sama dengan kami,” ungkap Peter dikutip, Sabtu (29/8/2026).
Menurut Peter, setelah mengetahui kompetisi IPL berlangsung, PB PTMSI telah menyampaikan surat kepada jajaran Pengurus Provinsi (Pengprov) yang berada di bawah organisasinya.
Surat tersebut, kata dia, diteruskan kepada pengurus tenis meja tingkat kabupaten/kota hingga klub-klub.
Langkah itu ditempuh karena atlet pada umumnya bernaung di bawah klub sebagai bagian dari struktur pembinaan.
“Sudah, kita sudah bersurat ke anggota kita, pengurus provinsi ya tentu sudah meneruskan ke kabupaten-kota dan klub-klub yang ada. Di mana, atlet itu kan semuanya bernaung di bawah klub,” katanya.
Ancaman Sanksi Membayangi Atlet
Persoalan menjadi lebih kompleks ketika PB PTMSI memilih jalur sanksi terhadap atlet yang mengikuti kompetisi IPL.
Peter menyatakan atlet yang tampil dalam kegiatan IPL berpotensi tidak memperoleh rekomendasi untuk mengikuti kejuaraan yang berada di bawah PB PTMSI.
items.normalised_title: di tengah friksi pb ptmsi dan ipl nasib atlet tenis meja ikut terdampak

Empat calon Ketum PBNU sepakat memakai AHWA, tetapi peserta muktamar menolak. Sidang deadlock dan voting jadi jalan keluar.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Empat calon Ketua Umum PBNU mengusulkan mekanisme pemilihan melalui Ahlul Halli wal Aqdi (AHWA) jika musyawarah mufakat tidak tercapai.
- Sebagian peserta Muktamar ke-35 NU menginginkan Ketua Umum tetap dipilih langsung oleh muktamirin yang memiliki hak suara.
- Perbedaan pandangan membuat pembahasan buntu. Forum kemudian menyepakati voting untuk menjaring maksimal lima calon sebelum nama-nama tersebut diserahkan kepada AHWA.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JOMBANG - Pemilihan Ketua Umum Pengurus Besar Nahdlatul Ulama (PBNU) periode 2026-2031 dalam Muktamar ke-35 NU mengalami kebuntuan setelah peserta berbeda pandangan soal mekanisme pemilihan.
Empat calon Ketua Umum PBNU mengusulkan agar pemilihan dilakukan melalui Ahlul Halli wal Aqdi (AHWA) apabila musyawarah mufakat tidak tercapai.
Keempat calon tersebut yakni KH Zulfa Mustofa, KH Abdul Hakim Mahfudz atau Gus Kikin, KH Muhammad Yusuf Chudlori atau Gus Yusuf, dan KH Abdul Ghaffar Rozin atau Gus Rozin.
Usulan itu disampaikan KH Zulfa Mustofa dalam pembahasan mekanisme pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU di Muktamar ke-35 NU di Pondok Pesantren Bahrul Ulum Tambakberas, Jombang, Jawa Timur, Sabtu (29/8/2026).
Zulfa mengatakan para calon tersebut telah sepakat dengan mekanisme AHWA jika musyawarah mufakat tidak tercapai.
Namun, usulan tersebut mendapat penolakan dari sebagian peserta muktamar. Mereka menginginkan Ketua Umum PBNU tetap dipilih oleh muktamirin atau peserta muktamar yang memiliki hak suara.
Perbedaan pandangan itu membuat pembahasan mekanisme pemilihan tidak mencapai kesepakatan atau deadlock.
Forum kemudian menyepakati pemungutan suara atau voting sebagai tahap untuk menjaring calon Ketua Umum PBNU.
Baca juga: Kandidat Ketum PBNU Terkuat Dinilai Tinggal 2 Orang: Gus Kikin dan Gus Yahya
Voting Jaring Lima Calon
Dalam rumusan mekanisme yang dibacakan Katib Syuriyah PBNU Prof KH M Asrorun Ni'am Sholeh bersama KH Mohammad Nuh, musyawarah mufakat tetap ditempatkan sebagai prinsip utama pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU.
Apabila mufakat tidak tercapai, proses pemilihan dilanjutkan melalui AHWA.
Namun, sebelum nama calon diserahkan kepada AHWA, muktamirin terlebih dahulu melakukan voting untuk menjaring calon Ketua Umum.
Setiap peserta yang memiliki hak suara dapat memilih maksimal lima nama calon yang memenuhi persyaratan.
Lima nama dengan perolehan suara terbanyak kemudian ditetapkan sebagai calon Ketua Umum PBNU untuk diserahkan kepada AHWA.
"Calon ketua umum sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat empat yang sudah dipilih oleh muktamirin tadi dipilih oleh Ahlul Halli wal Aqdi," kata Asrorun Ni'am saat membacakan rumusan di hadapan peserta pleno.
Dengan mekanisme tersebut, peserta muktamar tetap memiliki peran dalam menjaring kandidat, sedangkan pemilihan akhir dilakukan melalui AHWA apabila musyawarah mufakat tidak tercapai.

items.title: Wamendagri Ribka Tekankan Indonesia Timur Punya Peran Penting Wujudkan Indonesia Emas 2045
items.summary: Wamendagri Ribka Haluk menegaskan bahwa Indonesia Timur memiliki peran penting dalam mewujudkan visi Indonesia Emas 2045.
items.body_text:
Wamendagri Ribka Tekankan Indonesia Timur Punya Peran Penting Wujudkan Indonesia Emas 2045
Wamendagri Ribka Haluk menegaskan bahwa Indonesia Timur memiliki peran penting dalam mewujudkan visi Indonesia Emas 2045.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM – Wakil Menteri Dalam Negeri (Wamendagri) Ribka Haluk menegaskan bahwa Indonesia Timur memiliki peran penting dalam mewujudkan visi Indonesia Emas 2045. Menurutnya, potensi sumber daya alam dan masyarakat di kawasan tersebut perlu dioptimalkan dengan meningkatkan daya saing dan kesejahteraan, serta mendukung berbagai program pembangunan nasional.
Ribka mengatakan, dengan jumlah penduduk sekitar 286 juta jiwa dan ditopang bonus demografi, Indonesia memiliki modal besar untuk mewujudkan visi tersebut. Namun, potensi itu perlu dikelola dengan baik agar besarnya jumlah penduduk usia produktif benar-benar memberikan manfaat bagi pembangunan.
"Kita sedang ada dalam bonus demografi. Artinya usia produktif jumlah persentasenya cukup tinggi dibanding dengan umur di bawah 15 tahun dan di atas 60 tahun. Kita sedang Indonesia sudah memiliki bonus demografi. Ini betul-betul harus kita pastikan diri menjadi produktif," ungkapnya saat memberikan keynote speech pada National Building Conference Tahun 2026 di Gedung Dome Harvest, Lippo Karawaci, Tangerang, Banten, Sabtu (29/8/2026).
Menurut Ribka, pengelolaan bonus demografi membutuhkan peran pemerintah sekaligus dukungan seluruh elemen masyarakat. Karena itu, berbagai program prioritas nasional di bawah kepemimpinan Presiden melalui Asta Cita perlu didukung agar manfaatnya dapat dirasakan masyarakat.
Program tersebut antara lain Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), swasembada pangan melalui pemanfaatan lahan pertanian dan lumbung pangan, pembangunan infrastruktur, pembangunan sekolah-sekolah yang terintegrasi, hingga upaya menurunkan angka kemiskinan.
"Justru kita harus berterima kasih pada Pak Presiden yang ingin memperbaiki kualitas kehidupan masyarakat. Malah pemerintah daerah harus lebih giat supaya program ini sampai berjalan tadi. Ini sebenarnya program yang sangat baik," jelasnya.
Dalam konteks pembangunan Indonesia Timur, Ribka kemudian menyoroti pelaksanaan Proyek Strategis Nasional (PSN) di Papua. Menurutnya, pembangunan berbagai infrastruktur di wilayah tersebut masih menghadapi sejumlah tantangan di lapangan sehingga membutuhkan dukungan masyarakat dan kolaborasi berbagai pihak.
Baca juga: Tinjau Korban Dugaan Keracunan MBG di Jayapura, Wamendagri Ribka Minta Pengawasan Diperketat
Selain pembangunan infrastruktur, Ribka menekankan pentingnya meningkatkan daya saing masyarakat, khususnya di Indonesia Timur. Upaya tersebut diperlukan untuk memperluas kesempatan masyarakat dalam meningkatkan kualitas hidup sekaligus menekan tingkat kemiskinan.
"Karena kantong-kantong kemiskinan di Indonesia cukup banyak ya, kita mengharapkan kesejahteraan," tambahnya.
Ribka menegaskan, pembangunan tidak semata-mata berorientasi pada pertumbuhan ekonomi, tetapi juga harus mampu meningkatkan kesejahteraan masyarakat. Upaya tersebut perlu ditopang dengan penerapan prinsip good governance, yang terdiri dari partisipasi, transparansi, responsivitas, supremasi hukum, akuntabilitas, visi strategis, efektivitas dan efisiensi, keadilan dan kesetaraan, konsensus, serta profesionalisme dan integritas.
Sebagai informasi, acara ini turut dihadiri oleh anggota DPD RI Dapil Papua Barat Filep Wamafma, Wakil Ketua I DPR Provinsi Papua Tengah Diben Elaby, anggota Dewan Energi Nasional (DEN) Johni Jonatan Numberi, Ketua Umum Cendekiawan Perempuan Papua Rosaline Irene Rumaseuw, serta Ketua Sekolah Tinggi Teologi (STT) Internasional Harvest Indonesia Daniel Runtuwene.

items.summary: A commitment to the Philippine government to remove harmful artificial intelligence (AI)-generated deepfakes from its platforms and cooperate with investigations on cybercrime and other online threats has been made by American technology firm Meta Platforms Inc., which owns Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. ...Keep on reading: Meta sharing FB, IG, WhatsApp info to help PH probe threats
items.body_text:
Meta sharing FB, IG, WhatsApp info to help PH probe threats
MANILA, Philippines — A commitment to the Philippine government to remove harmful artificial intelligence (AI)-generated deepfakes from its platforms and cooperate with investigations on cybercrime and other online threats has been made by American technology firm Meta Platforms Inc., which owns Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
Meta policy officials handling the Asia-Pacific region met with a Philippine delegation on Thursday in Singapore to discuss details of the company’s commitment in the wake of violent incidents that local officials suspect stemmed from social media content.
Secretary Henry Aguda of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) was among those who attended the meeting with Director Melvin Matibag of the National Bureau of Investigation, Laguna Rep. Ann Matibag who chairs the House committee on women, and representatives from the office of Sen. Risa Hontiveros.

READ: SiloyAsks: Netizens split on proposed social media ban for minors
“We were able to convince Meta to commit to providing our authorities with subscriber information and traffic data once they identify a threat to the safety of our children, even before an actual attack takes place,” Hontiveros said in a video message on Friday.
READ: Deepfakes, coordinated online harassment are public order concerns – PNP
Online risks
She said the “parallel development” will further gain traction for Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act, which seeks to regulate children’s access to social media platforms. The bill sets 16 years as the minimum age for social media use.
SB 2424, which was sponsored in plenary on Wednesday, will also obligate social media companies to protect minors from various online risks.
READ: PNP to track down internet users generating, sharing malicious deepfakes
In a Viber message to the Inquirer, Aguda outlined Meta’s commitment, including the establishment of a technical working group with the Philippine government to improve coordination, response times, and action on harmful content; the designation of a point of contact to facilitate faster response time; and the sharing of crucial data when necessary.
‘Good step’
Aguda said Meta also pledged continued cooperation with Philippine investigations, “particularly (on) cases involving imminent harm to children or risk of death or serious physical injury.”
A team from Meta is expected to visit Manila in mid-September to formalize the framework and commitments made.
Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian welcomed the development as a “good step.”
But it doesn’t mean that the Senate will no longer push for SB 2424, which also proposes that Meta set up a Philippine office, he told the Inquirer in a phone interview.
“So if there’s a problem, we can easily coordinate with them and we can prevent future problems,” he said.
Gatchalian added that a bill will make it easier to penalize social media companies for violations, citing the case in the United States where Meta was slapped with a multistate lawsuit accusing it of intentionally designing addictive social media platforms that harm children’s mental health.
The company entered into a landmark $18-billion settlement this month to resolve the cases.
But because there is no law in the Philippines yet, he said, it would be difficult to make social media companies accountable for harmful content.
“For example, what happened in Zamboanga, the was uploaded and they did not stop it. They could be penalized [if a law exists],” Gatchalian said. The senator was referring to the video of the Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting earlier this month that was uploaded on Facebook but was not immediately taken down.

items.body_text:
‘Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang,’ ‘Sister Stella L’ to lead PFIM 2026 screenings
With the theme “Pelikula: Ginintuang Ikalawa,” this year’s celebration of the Philippine Film Industry Month (PFIM) will feature screenings of digitally restored classics including Lino Brocka’s “Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang” and Mike de Leon’s “Sister Stella L,” among others.
The Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP) announced PFIM’s monthlong activities that celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema.
The screening of “Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang” will kick off the celebration at the Red Carpet Cinema, Shangri-La Plaza on Sept. 4, along with the announcement of the Philippines’ entry to the 2027 Oscars Best International Feature Film category.
Other digitally restored classics — including de Leon’s “Itim,” Brocka’s “Insiang,” Mario O’Hara’s “Tatlong Taong Walang Diyos,” Lupita Aquino-Kashiwahara’s “Minsa’y Isang Gamu-Gamo,” Eddie Romero’s “Ganito Kami Noon… Paano Kayo Ngayon?” and Ishmael Bernal’s “Nunal sa Tubig” — will be showcased throughout the month at FDCP Cinematheque Centres nationwide.
The audiences will also be taken further back in time with the “SineUna: Cinematic Action Before the War,” which will feature Eduardo de Castro’s “Zamboanga,” Carlos Vander Tolosa’s “Giliw Ko,” Vicente Salumbide’s “Ibong Adarna” and Octavio Silos’ “Tunay na Ina” and “Pakiusap.”
Meanwhile, the newly digitally-restored “Sister Stella L” will have its grand homecoming on Sept. 20 at the Metropolitan Theater as part of the “Mga Hiyas ng Sineng Pilipino,” which is co-presented by the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA).
READ: FDCP sets 1st Nat’l Cinema Day in Sept. with aim to bring audiences back to theaters
Other key PFIM 2026 events include the “Reel to Real: Pelikula at Panayam,” which will spotlight Brocka’s “Jaguar”; the Director’s Series, which will feature Jeffrey Jeturian’s “Tuhog” and “Kubrador”; the world premiere of Mike Alcazaren’s documentary film “Kodomo-tachi: Children of the War” on Sept. 17; the inaugural edition of the PFIM Short Film Competition; Sine Kabataan 2026; and the return of the Film Education Convention (FilmEc).
The PFIM 2026 will conclude with a closing ceremony on Sept. 30. /ra

Sarah Geronimo madbos? Matteo nakadawat og ‘soon-to-be daddy’ greeting
Mga netizens naghunahuna nga mabdos si Sarah Geronimo human ang iyang asawa, ang aktor nga si Matteo Guidicelli, nakadawat og “soon-to-be daddy” congratulatory greeting sa usa ka nagpa-ila nga amigo.
Usa ka Facebook user, nga amigo ni Guidicelli, ang nag-post og hulagway nila sa aktor nga karon gi-delete na. Matod pa niya, kuha ang maong photo dihang nag-abot sila sa usa ka coffee shop sa Quezon City
“Deep in a meeting with a colleague, totally unaware someone familiar was right there until Gianmatteo Guidecilli walked up and said, ‘ka-ila gyud ko ani!’ (I know this person!)” segon pa sa giingon amigo. “Truly caught me by surprise! So many shared memories with Matt —from shoots, Airborne Proficiency Jumps, and our days at ISAFP. Solid guy — hindi mayabang, sobrang friendly pa.”

(Sa ka focus nako sa usa ka meeting sa akong kauban, wala ko kabantay nga naa koy kaiila nga naa sa [cafe] hangtod nidoul siya ug nag-sulti, ‘Ka-ila man gyod ko ani! […] Tinoud nakuratan ko! Daghan kaayo mig kaagi ni Matt — gikan sa mga shoots, Airborne Proficiency Jumps, ug sa among mga adlaw sa ISAFP. Saligan gyud na nga tawo — di hambugero, ug friendly pa gyod kaayo.)

items.title: FULL INTERVIEW: Mike Dizon on drumming for 3 bands, love for food
items.summary: Dizon sits down with Rappler to talk about his beginnings in music, what it's like for him to move from genre to genre as the drummer of TEETH, Sandwich, and Pedicab, and how he discovered his love for documenting the restaurants he comes across
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – It’s not every day that an artist finds himself being a part of three of the Philippines’ most influential bands at the same time, until you meet Mike Dizon.
Dizon co-founded the alternative rock and grunge outfit TEETH in 1993. Years later, he also began playing the drums for rock band Sandwich and electronic rock band Pedicab. He is also a prolific songwriter, and is the mind behind hit songs like “Laklak” and “Prinsesa” by TEETH.
Outside of music, though, Dizon runs a successful YouTube channel, where he visits local eateries to try out the best dishes on the menu.
Ahead of TEETH’s reunion concert tour in celebration of their 33 years as a band, Dizon sits down with Rappler to talk about his beginnings in music, what it’s like for him to move from genre to genre, and how he discovered his love for documenting the restaurants he comes across.
Catch the full interview at 7 pm on Saturday, August 29, by bookmarking this page or heading to Rappler’s YouTube! – Rappler.com

items.title: Judicial and Bar Council opens application for next Supreme Court chief justice
items.summary: Marcos will get to pick the next chief justice after Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo's retirement in November
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) on Saturday, August 29, announced the opening of application for the next Supreme Court (SC) chief justice due to the upcoming retirement of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.
The new chief magistrate, who will be chosen by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., will replace Gesmundo who will retire on November 6. Under the rule, justices are mandated to retire from the judiciary when they reach the age of 70.
The next chief magistrate will be the country’s 28th Chief Justice and will sit at the SC’s top post. The High Court oversees all courts in the country, including high level courts like the Sandiganbayan, Court of Appeals, and the Court of Tax Appeals.
Gesmundo has been the chief justice since April 2021 upon the appointment of former president Rodrigo Duterte. Sources and court people alike often refer to Gesmundo as the High Court’s “stabilizing force” for introducing a concept of collegiality among the justices and reforms inside the SC.
Meanwhile, Gesmundo’s replacement will be chosen by Marcos after a screening process to be led by JBC. Public interviews will be held as well as part of this process.
Apart from Gesmundo, Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier is also retiring in November.
This gives Marcos two new appointments to the High Court after his first pick in 2025, Associate Justice Raul Villanueva. (READ: IN NUMBERS: Things to know about the Philippine Supreme Court and its justices)
Once Gesmundo and Lazaro Javier retire, the Duterte appointees inside the SC will drop to 10; Marcos might have three, while former president Benigno Aquino III has two. – Rappler.com

items.title: Monsoon rain due to enhanced southwest monsoon affecting 12 areas in Luzon
items.summary: The enhanced southwest monsoon or habagat is bringing monsoon rain to Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, and Cavite
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- At least 12 areas in Luzon are experiencing monsoon rain due to the enhanced southwest monsoon, with heavy rain expected to continue over the weekend.
- Two low pressure areas (LPAs) are being monitored, one with a low chance and another with a high chance of developing into a tropical depression, which will be named Pilandok upon entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
- PAGASA has issued heavy rainfall outlooks for various regions, warning residents in low-lying areas to be vigilant against potential floods and landslides.
MANILA, Philippines – At least 12 areas in Luzon are experiencing monsoon rain on Saturday afternoon, August 29, as the enhanced southwest monsoon or habagat continues to affect the island.
On Saturday morning, the low pressure area (LPA) previously inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility was already located outside PAR. It was last located 640 kilometers north northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, with a “low” chance of developing into a tropical depression.
Another LPA being monitored outside PAR, which has a “high” chance of developing into a tropical depression, was last located 1,545 km east of extreme Northern Luzon. Once it enters PAR and strengthens, it will be called the local name Pilandok.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) reported monsoon rain due to the enhanced southwest monsoon in Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, and Cavite.
The southwest monsoon is also bringing occasional rain to Ilocos Norte, Abra, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Laguna, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Oriental Mindoro, scattered rain and thunderstorms to the rest of Luzon, Western Visayas, and Negros Island Region, and isolated rain showers or thunderstorms to the rest of Visayas.
PAGASA Weather Specialist Daniel James Villamil said heavy rain will continue to affect Metro Manila, most of Central Luzon, and portions of Southern Luzon over the weekend and until Monday. By Monday, there will be a shift in rainfall distribution, with heavy rain affecting Northern Luzon.
Below is PAGASA’s latest heavy rainfall outlook due to the southwest monsoon in the next three days:
Saturday afternoon, August 29, to Sunday afternoon, August 30:
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, and Cavite
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Ilocos Norte, Abra, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Laguna, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Oriental Mindoro
Sunday afternoon, August 30, to Monday afternoon, August 31:
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro
Monday afternoon, August 31, to Tuesday afternoon, September 1
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, and Zambales
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, and Cavite

items.title: 32 dead, 8 million affected by 'Luis,' 'Maymay,' 'Neneng,' habagat — OCD
items.summary: At least 32 people have died while around 8 million people have been affected by tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the southwest monsoon or habagat, the Office of Civil Defense said Saturday, August 29.
items.body_text:
32 dead, 8 million affected by 'Luis,' 'Maymay,' 'Neneng,' habagat — OCD
MANILA, Philippines — At least 32 people have died while around 8 million people have been affected by tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the southwest monsoon or habagat, the Office of Civil Defense said Saturday, August 29.
In its latest situation report, the OCD said the weather disturbances have affected around 2.3 million families or 8 million individuals across the country.
Benguet recorded the highest number of fatalities at 15, all due to landslides.
The OCD also reported six deaths in Rizal, four in Batangas, two each in Occidental Mindoro and Caloocan, and one each in La Union, Quezon, Oriental Mindoro and Negros Occidental.
The reported deaths were due to drowning, landslides, rockslides, fallen trees and electrocution.
The disaster agency also recorded 19 injured individuals, while three people remain missing — one each from Quezon City, Manila and Batangas.
Meanwhile, at least 25,800 people remain in evacuation centers due to the effects of the weather disturbances.
Nearly 3,000 houses were damaged, including 349 that were totally destroyed.
Infrastructure damage has reached P6.11 billion, while agricultural damage was estimated at P2.32 billion, according to the OCD.
At least 117 local government units have declared a state of calamity.
The government has so far extended P1.65 billion worth of assistance to affected communities.
Rainfall warnings
Meanwhile, several areas in Luzon remained under rainfall warnings on Saturday afternoon as the southwest monsoon continued to bring heavy rains.
Metro Manila and several provinces were under a red rainfall warning, with PAGASA warning of serious flooding in flood-prone areas.
Under the red warning level were Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Tarlac, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Cavite, Rizal and parts of Batangas.
Other areas were placed under orange and yellow rainfall warnings, with flooding also threatening or possible in flood-prone areas.
LPA monitoring
As of 2 p.m. Saturday, PAGASA was monitoring two low pressure areas outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
One LPA had a low chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours, while the other had a high chance of developing within the same period.

items.title: Phivolcs warns of possible lahar flows from Pinatubo, Taal volcanoes amid habagat
items.summary: Phivolcs warned of possible lahar and volcanic debris flows from Mt. Pinatubo and Taal Volcano as heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or habagat continue to affect parts of Luzon.
items.body_text:
Phivolcs warns of possible lahar flows from Pinatubo, Taal volcanoes amid habagat
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) on Saturday, August 29, warned of possible lahar and volcanic debris flows from Mt. Pinatubo and Taal Volcano as heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or habagat continue to affect parts of Luzon.
Heavy rains may trigger lahars, muddy streamflows and runoff in rivers and drainage areas, according to Phivolcs advisory.
“Prolonged and intense rainfall may generate non-eruption lahars on major rivers draining western Pinatubo Volcano where significant deposits of the 1991 pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) remain on the watershed,” Phivolcs said.
Lahar flows from Pinatubo are likely to remain confined to channels along the upper to middle reaches of the Sto. Tomas-Marella and Bucao river systems, the agency said.
The flows may transition into muddy streamflows and flooding in the lower reaches, potentially affecting communities in San Marcelino, San Narciso, San Felipe and Botolan in Zambales.
Muddy streamflows may also develop along the O'Donnell and Pasig-Potrero river systems, which drain Pinatubo toward the north and southeast, respectively.
Downstream communities in Tarlac and Pampanga could be affected.
Taal Volcano
Phivolcs also warned of possible muddy streamflows, runoff and volcanic debris flows around Taal Volcano, particularly on the slopes west and north of Taal Lake.
“Prolonged and heavy rainfall may also generate muddy streamflow, muddy runoff and even volcanic debris flows around Taal Volcano, particularly on the slopes west and north of Taal Lake,” it said.
Loose volcanic deposits that have become saturated from previous rains could be remobilized through streams, roads and lakeward slopes.
Muddy and debris flows could recur in Agoncillo, Laurel and Talisay in Batangas, Phivolcs said.
The agency urged communities and local government units in the identified areas to continue monitoring weather conditions and take preemptive measures to ensure the safety of residents.
The warning comes as the southwest monsoon continues to bring heavy rains over parts of Luzon, with several areas placed under rainfall warnings on Saturday.

items.title: Vietnam and US begin talks on roadmap for concrete partnership results, ambassador says
items.summary: Vietnam and the U.S. have begun discussions on a roadmap to translate their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership into concrete and measurable outcomes across a broad range of areas, U.S. Ambassador to Vietnam Jennifer Wicks said at a press roundtable in Hanoi on Aug. 28.
items.body_text:
Responding to a question on how the two countries could make their upgraded partnership more substantive and results-oriented, the ambassador said the two sides share similar thinking on what the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership should mean in practice, including the specific activities and projects needed to give substance to the relationship.
As an example, she pointed to the recent successful visit by the USS George Washington aircraft carrier to Vietnam’s central coastal city of Da Nang. The bilateral partnership, she said, has a forward-looking agenda spanning politics, security, law enforcement, the economy, health, education and people-to-people ties, with the broader goal of advancing prosperity and security for both peoples.
She noted that the approaching third anniversary of the establishment of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership provides a timely opportunity to advance the bilateral relationship further.
Economic and commercial cooperation is among the ambassador’s major priorities during her tenure. Wicks said she will advocate for U.S. companies and the private sector while working to ensure that Vietnamese authorities and consumers are aware of the high-quality products and services that U.S. businesses can offer. Since arriving in Vietnam, she said she has already engaged on opportunities in sectors including aviation, energy, technology and defense.
The ambassador also welcomed the Vietnamese Government’s willingness to engage with the U.S. side and American companies on concerns related to market access and regulatory and other business challenges, with a view to ensuring a level playing field for U.S. firms.
On defense and security cooperation, the ambassador highlighted the progress the two countries have made from addressing the legacies of war to working together in wider areas of shared interest.
She described war legacy programmes as an important foundation for the growing trust between Vietnam and the U.S., saying they demonstrate how Vietnamese and Americans can work side by side towards common goals.
Asked about future cooperation in identifying the missing, she said the U.S. support could draw on government resources and technology as well as expertise from the private sector and educational institutions.
Education and people-to-people exchanges are another important pillar of the relationship and Vietnam ranks first in ASEAN and among the leading countries worldwide in the number of students studying in the U.S., according to the ambassador.
Concluding the roundtable, the ambassador pledged to work to advance the two countries’ shared interests and achieve positive outcomes for both Vietnam and the U.S.

items.title: First-year international applications to US colleges drop 10% amid policy shifts
items.summary: Applications from first-year international students to U.S. universities fell about 10% in the 2025-26 admissions cycle, ending nearly a decade of growth as interest weakened across major source regions, according to a new report.
items.body_text:
The number of first-year international students applying to U.S. universities fell to 148,780 in the 2025-26 admissions cycle, a decline of roughly 16,000 from the previous year, according to the Common Application, better known as Common App, a centralized online platform that allows undergraduate students to apply to 1,146 colleges and universities across all 50 U.S. states and several other countries.
The Common App 2025-26 End-of-Season Report indicates the decline was broad-based across much of the world, with applicants from Asia falling 11% and those from Africa dropping 17%.
The downturn follows years of strong growth for U.S. higher education. Common App data showed first-year international applicants increased steadily from 80,312 in the 2014-2015 academic year to 96,320 in 2018-2019.
Following a brief pandemic-driven dip in 2019-2020, the number rebounded to 107,112 in 2020-2021 and continued to grow until slightly dropping in 2024-2025.
This international downturn, however, runs counter to domestic trends, as the number of U.S. first-year applicants increased by 4%.
The figures highlight the impact of the Trump administration's restrictive immigration policies.
During the 2025-26 admissions cycle, prospective students faced heightened scrutiny over visas and immigration rules.
These U.S. policies have created greater uncertainty by imposing entry restrictions affecting nationals of 39 countries, disrupting visa processing during the peak season, and enforcing a new four-year maximum stay starting Sept. 15.
The administration has also signaled plans to reform the Optional Practical Training program, a crucial pathway for international STEM graduates to gain temporary work experience in the U.S.
Rodney Hughes, a senior data scientist at Common App, said: "We have thought about what's been going on over the past season and it's interesting to differentiate the applicants, which is what we see here, from enrollments and just the thought process of applying."
"If you think, 'OK, it might be hard for me to get a visa,' that may make students more hesitant to apply," he said, as quoted by Inside Higher Ed.
According to a joint analysis by NAFSA: Association of International Educators and JB International, the U.S. could lose up to $3.4 billion in economic activity and nearly 40,000 jobs next academic year as international student enrollment declines.
The analysis draws on the Institute of International Education's (IIE) Spring 2026 Snapshot, which surveyed 585 U.S. higher education institutions.
IIE projects a 9.5% decline in overall international student enrollment for the 2026-27 academic year, attributing the expected drop to "visa delays, policy uncertainties, and growing global competition."
Based on the projection, about 111,000 fewer international students are expected to enroll at U.S. colleges and universities next year. Total enrollment is projected to fall to 1.057 million, from an estimated 1.169 million in 2025-26.
